Miranda Cachini, 27, had pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter in the 2-month-old’s death in January 2025. Her attorney did not return calls for comment Thursday.

description: An experienced Oregon pilot who mentored countless others, a 22-year-old flight instructor from Texas and a student pilot from the United Kingdom were killed when their two helicopters collided in Oregon. Thirty-eight-year-old Tyler Sturdevant had worked for more than 20 years at Precision, a helicopter charter and maintenance company. In a post on social media, the company remembered him for his passion for flying and dedication to helping other pilots succeed. Maddie Aasbo was instructing 31-year-old Christopher Joughin, a student pilot, when the two helicopters slammed into each other Thursday near an airport southwest of Portland. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash.

The crash has forced a portion of Highway 233 to close. The Yamhill County Sheriff's Office says the crash Thursday killed a  38-year-old pilot from Oregon, a 22-year-old flight instructor from Texas and student pilot from the United Kingdom. Officials say emergency crews responded around 2:15 p.m. following reports of a crash a few miles east of the McMinnville Airport. The Federal Aviation Administration says one of the helicopters was carrying only the pilot and the other one had two people aboard. The Oregon Department of Transportation says Highway 233 is closed 1 mile west of Dayton.

Democrats are speeding toward a tug-of-war between establishment leaders eyeing control of Congress and emboldened progressives demanding nothing less than transformative change. description: The Vatican is opening a celebration of the popemobile. The now-iconic vehicle has allowed popes to get close to the faithful at home and abroad for nearly a century. The Vatican Museums unveiled a preview of the exhibition on Wednesday commemorating “A Century of the Popemobile.” It features eight Mercedes-Benz versions of the car that popes have used since 1930. Pope Leo XIV is a big car lover. He separately met with top Mercedes-Benz executives and thanked them for their partnership with the Holy See. The Chicago-born pope noted in his remarks that the advances in automotive technology had accompanied the advances and evolutions of papal travel. The exhibition officially opens to the public on Thursday.
headline: A popemobile exhibition at the Vatican features the vehicle popes have used since 1930

description: An appeals court has declined to rule on whether California elections officials can count roughly 20,000 ballots that the Justice Department alleges likely belong to noncitizen voters. Monday's decision sets the federal government and state officials up for another legal showdown Tuesday before a federal district judge. That gives the federal government a very short window to compel California to sequester votes before the Nov. 3 elections. The Republican administration sued election officials in the heavily Democratic state in mid-October, accusing them of failing to meet a 48-hour deadline to review a list of 20,000 people it alleged were likely noncitizens on the state’s voter rolls. The Justice Department didn’t immediately respond to an emailed inquiry about Monday's decision.

description: A federal appeals court has rejected the Justice Department’s request for California to set aside disputed ballots received in the midterm election. The panel’s 2-1 ruling Friday is the latest setback for the Trump administration’s efforts to assert control over state-run elections. The administration has alleged California sent ballots to some 20,000 people who may not be U.S. citizens. In a separate ruling Friday, another federal judge barred the department from intimidating election workers involved in processing those ballots. The Justice Department did not immediately comment on either ruling.
headline: Appeals court rejects Justice Department request for California to set aside disputed ballots

description: Lancaster County in Pennsylvania has been the epicenter of the nation's worst measles outbreak in 35 years. It's also home to the largest Amish population in the U.S. Some Amish and related Mennonite groups, with historically lower rates of vaccination, have been hit hard. Vaccination rates also declined in the general population amid the resurgence of a contagious virus considered “eliminated” from the U.S. since 2000. Pennsylvania leads the U.S. this year with over 1,350 cases, more than a third in Lancaster County, according to official figures. Many Amish and Mennonites are showing a new openness to vaccines, while members of the general public are also taking extra precautions.
headline: As a historic measles outbreak hits Pennsylvania Amish country, more show openness to vaccines

author: ROB MAADDI
description: Just three outs from winning the first World Series title in franchise history, the Milwaukee Brewers’ bullpen finally faltered. Left-hander Aaron Ashby retired all seven batters he faced in Game 4 against Tampa Bay and broke Andrew Miller’s record for scoreless innings by a reliever in one postseason. But manager Pat Murphy pulled Ashby with one out in the 11th. Murphy had used six pitchers already and turned to Antonio Senzatela, who got two outs to finish that inning. The right-hander began the 12th with a one-run lead after rookie Cooper Pratt put the Brewers ahead 3-2 with a solo homer, but an error by third baseman Joey Ortiz helped the Rays start their winning rally.
headline: Brewers' bullpen cracks in Game 4 loss after Aaron Ashby breaks postseason scoreless relief mark

author: ZAK GILBERT
description: Robert Gasser delivered in the World Series unlike any left-handed starter since Sandy Koufax. Gasser faced the minimum over six dominant innings, pitching the Milwaukee Brewers to the brink of their first championship in a 10-1 win over the Tampa Bay Rays. He’s the first starter to face the minimum over six innings in a World Series game since Curt Schilling for the Arizona Diamondbacks in Game 7 of the 2001 Fall Classic.
headline: Brewers' Robert Gasser spins World Series gem unlike any by a lefty since Sandy Koufax

author: ROB MAADDI
description: Jackson Chourio and Brice Turang sparked Milwaukee's eight-run fifth inning, and the Brewers routed the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 to move within one victory of their first World Series title. Rookie left-hander Robert Gasser pitched one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings as Milwaukee rolled to a 3-0 lead in the Series. Game 4 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, where many Brewers fans showed up Monday and cheered from behind the visitors’ dugout. Gasser allowed a line-drive single to Yandy Díaz leading off the bottom of the first and then retired 14 straight before Victor Mesa Jr. walked to start the Tampa Bay sixth.
headline: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title

author: Taylor Croft
description: Three people are accused of planning a school shooting attack to take place August 20, 2027, at Cherokee High School, Canton police said Tuesday.
headline: 3 arrested for Cherokee school shooting plans had set date, made checklist

author: CYBELE MAYES-OSTERMAN
description: A thwarted mass shooting at a Hindu temple near Chicago is stoking new fears for the area’s South Asian community, tainting a typically joyful season of faith and family gatherings. Members of the targeted temple and others in the area say they are seeking comfort in preserving traditions, determined to celebrate the holidays without fear. Nineteen-year-old Alexandros Paporakis is due back in court on charges he planned to commit a mass shooting at a temple in Aurora, Illinois, on the first day of the festival of Navaratri. South Asian leaders are pressing for hate crime charges to be added to the charges he faces.
headline: Chicago-area Hindu community shaken but resilient after alleged mass shooting plan was thwarted

author: Caroline Silva
description: A woman has been arrested after a child was found dead Monday evening as police conducted a wellness check at a southwest Atlanta residence, officials say.
headline: Boy, 4, found in SW Atlanta died from blunt force injuries, officials say

description: China's factory activity contracted in October, reversing the previous month's reboujnd. The National Bureau of Statistics reported Saturday that the official purchasing managers' index fell to 49.3, down from 50.1 in September. A PMI below 50 indicates contraction. Key subindexes, like new export orders and production, also showed declines. Chinese companies have been exporting more due to weakened domestic demand, but this has led to complaints from trading partners about trade deficits. The European Union has been particularly vocal with demands to rebalance trade. Some economists have predicted China's exports will remain strong for the rest of this year despite ongoing trade tensions.
headline: China’s factory activity slips as new export orders weaken

author: Sean Tucker
description: Chinese automakers are largely blocked from selling cars in the United States. But that may not be true forever.
headline: Opinion: What Americans should know about Chinese cars

author: KIM CHANDLER
description: Christa Pike says she is in constant pain since surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee last month. In her first public statement, issued Friday, she expressed gratitude for the love and support she has received. Pike says she went into the execution chamber prepared to die in peace but woke up confused in a hospital bed. She said she's been “deeply hurt by the incompetence.” Pike says she had not contemplated life beyond her execution date and is thankful for the medical workers who saved her. She says she is trying to heal and is holding on to the kindness of others.
headline: Christa Pike describes constant pain in first statement since her failed execution

author: AARON BEARD
description: The eligibility chaos playing out in lawsuits and courthouses all over the country has reached the basketball season. The first Division I men's and women's basketball games start Sunday. Yet that comes as legal cases tied to eligiblity inch their way through the court system. Many cases are centered on the NCAA's adoption of an age-based model giving athletes a fifth year going forward. Others deal with athletes returning to college after signing with professional teams. The cases have created volatility with players still waiting to be cleared or facing hearings that could change their status abruptly during the season.
headline: College basketball season is here. The eligibility chaos playing out in courthouses comes with it

author: MATTHEW LEE
description: Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies appeared far apart on critical global security issues as they began meeting in Atlanta. European objections to Russia’s participation forced the U.S. hosts to cancel a traditional group photo planned for Friday. That underscored deep rifts among the group over global crises that threaten international security and trade, such as Russia's war in Ukraine. Still, Rubio opened the meeting saying he hoped it can be productive. Diplomats who attended the opening session described it as cordial but said Russia's position on Ukraine remains unyielding.
headline: Consensus looks elusive at G20 talks after European objections to Russia cancel group photo

author: LEAH WILLINGHAM
description: Cornell University says it will review how it handled the co-ed housing assignment of a student who returned to campus after serving a suspension connected to an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house. A professor accused the university of a “dangerous disconnect” between its disciplinary and housing systems, saying housing officials were unaware of the student’s history and his roommate received no warning. The student’s identity and co-ed dorm location later circulated online, raising safety concerns. Cornell says students who complete suspensions regain their housing eligibility. The controversy raises broader questions about how universities balance student privacy, campus safety and the reintegration of disciplined students.
headline: Cornell faces questions over dorm assignment for student disciplined in sexual assault case

author: ANDREA RODRÍGUEZ
description: Cuba has welcomed home a diplomat expelled by the United States after a heated confrontation at the United Nations this week. Cuban Deputy Foreign Minister Gerardo Peñalver shared a photo of Richard Tur de la Concepción at Havana’s airport. The U.S. State Department announced Tur’s expulsion, accusing him of shoving an American diplomat and trying to snatch his phone. The incident escalated into a shouting match between U.S. Ambassador Mike Waltz and Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez. Tensions have deepened since U.S. President Donald Trump imposed an energy blockade on Cuba in January.
headline: Cuba welcomes home diplomat expelled from US after unusual altercation at the UN

author: GENE JOHNSON
description: The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration has for the first time issued registrations to medical marijuana businesses. It is a bureaucratic maneuver under President Donald Trump’s historic rescheduling of the drug that could pave the way for the dispensaries to receive tax benefits long denied the industry. The agency issued the registrations Friday to more than 900 state-licensed dispensaries in Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia and West Virginia, the Justice Department said in a news release. The department did not immediately identify the approved businesses.
headline: DEA approvals could bring big tax benefits for medical marijuana businesses

author: DANIEL KOZIN and MAURICIO SAVARESE
description: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family have landed in Miami after fleeing Brazil. Bolsonaro fled after he refused to concede the election to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Bolsonaro’s father Jair Bolsonaro also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula. The United States has granted visas to Flávio Bolsonaro and his family and U.S. President Donald Trump has questioned Brazil's election result. Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil’s Supreme Court, accused of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. He has denied those allegations. The Trump ally visited the White House in May.
headline: Defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family land in Miami after fleeing Brazil

author: Kelly Yamanouchi
description: Delta will take over the lease for Spirit's gates at Hartsfield-Jackson, possibly adding more flights and cutting down on tarmac traffic.
headline: Delta takeover of Spirit gates at Atlanta airport ratified by City Council

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: The Atlanta Dream say Thursday’s WNBA Finals Game 6 against the Golden State Valkyries is a sellout despite its much-criticized 12:30 p.m. Eastern tipoff. The Valkyries lead the series 3-2 and can clinch their first WNBA title with a win in the matinee at State Farm Arena. The Dream need a win to force a Game 7 on Saturday night in California. There were concerns the early tipoff would have the teams playing the potentially decisive Finals game in a half-empty arena because of fans having work and school obligations. Instead, another sellout of approximately 17,000 is expected.
headline: Despite much-criticized early tipoff, Dream say WNBA Finals Game 6 against Valkyries is a sellout

description: Los Angeles Dodgers executive Bob Wolfe is retiring at the end of the year after 14 years as executive vice president. Wolfe has also served as chief operating officer for the last five years, overseeing the team's day-to-day operations. He will transition to an advisory role with the club. Wolfe's 47-year career includes time with the NBA's Atlanta Hawks, and MLB's Atlanta Braves and Washington Nationals. He helped with the construction of Turner Field in Atlanta and Nationals Park in Washington.
headline: Dodgers executive Bob Wolfe to retire at year’s end, shifting to an advisory role

author: JOEY CAPPELLETTI and SIMRAN PARWANI
description: Early voting is surging ahead of Tuesday’s midterm elections, particularly in states with competitive Senate races. An Associated Press analysis shows more than 43 million Americans have already cast ballots, nearly 10 million more than at the same point in 2022. Texas has seen a 50% increase, with 6.3 million early votes cast. Maine, Michigan, North Carolina and Kansas have also recorded increases of more than 30%. The data offers a glimpse of early voter participation five days before an election that will determine control of Congress and other key contests across the country.
headline: Early voting jumps across Senate battlegrounds as millions more Americans vote ahead of Election Day

author: Kelly Yamanouchi
description: The tiff began with a Tuesday social media post on X about Delta's CEO and Starlink Wi-Fi service.
headline: Elon Musk knocks Delta CEO over inflight Wi-Fi. United sees an opening.

author: JOSH FUNK
description: The Environmental Protection Agency’s response to the disastrous 2023 East Palestine train derailment will be investigated after dozens of residents of the small town on the Ohio-Pennsylvania and Vice President JD Vance requested the review. The Inspector General of the EPA announced the investigation Tuesday to assess the agency’s response to the worst rail disaster in more than a decade. Resident Jami Wallace said she is glad the concerns raised by people who live in the area are getting attention again. She has tracked more than 80 cases of cancer among residents.
headline: EPA response to 2023 Ohio train derailment will be investigated by agency watchdog

author: JOE REEDY
description: Ernie Johnson is retiring as host of “Inside the NBA” in June, ending a 37-year run with the show. Johnson announced his decision Wednesday, saying, “It's just time.” He began hosting in 1990, and the program has won 21 Sports Emmy Awards. Johnson said he has been dealing with heart issues and wants to enjoy more time with family. Although the show has moved to ESPN, it remains produced by TNT. Johnson will continue hosting NCAA Tournament coverage and has started a new production company. His final appearance will be during the NBA Finals.
headline: Ernie Johnson to retire from 'Inside the NBA' in June after a 37-year run as host

author: ERIC TUCKER
description: Defense lawyers have urged a judge to dismiss a criminal complaint charging two former FBI counterintelligence officials with making false statements to Congress about Hunter Biden, calling the case an overtly political prosecution aimed at placating President Donald Trump. The arguments Thursday capped a days-long hearing in which lawyers for the former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides, sought to cast the case as legally defective and tainted by politics. The hearing included testimony that the investigation was ordered by FBI Director Kash Patel and that it was opened on the heels of a primetime election security speech by Trump in which the Republican rehashed long-running grievances about his 2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.
headline: Ex-FBI officials accused of false statements about Hunter Biden press for dismissal of charges

author: FRED GOODALL
description: Inconsistency and seemingly disastrous starts to this season in the NFC South have not undermined the aspirations of the Atlanta Falcons and Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It's a division won by teams finishing with losing records two of the past four seasons, including a year ago when Carolina, the Falcons and Bucs all went 8-9. The Panthers by tiebreaker claimed their first title since 2015 and currently sit atop the standings with a 3-3 record. Atlanta and Tampa Bay are lurking despite slow starts, with each hoping to bolster bids to take control of a wide-open race when the rivals meet Sunday. The Falcons are 3-4, while the Bucs enter 2-5.
headline: Falcons' Penix and Buccaneers' Mayfield aiming to help rebounding teams take control of NFC South

author: SARAH RAZA
description: An arson Saturday morning damaged the building of a beleaguered police department in Mississippi that has drawn outrage from the community in recent months after an officer shot and killed a 1-year-old, authorities said. The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and local agencies are investigating. The fire occurred around 4:30 a.m. at the Senatobia Police Department. It is the latest incident at the department. About a week ago an officer who shot and killed a 1-year-old boy in Mississippi when he fired into a moving vehicle while responding to a shoplifting call resigned, though he was cleared of criminal wrongdoing. In September, the police chief was fired after reporting that alleged he used racist slurs in private text messages.
headline: Federal officials investigate arson at beleaguered police department in Mississippi

author: Savannah Sicurella
description: The sentencing of Brant Frost IV was delivered on Monday afternoon in a federal courthouse mere steps from First Liberty Building & Loan’s former offices.
headline: First Liberty founder Brant Frost IV sentenced to 15 years in prison

author: DEE-ANN DURBIN
description: The U.S. Federal Trade Commission is ordering Delta Air Lines, Walmart and other companies to provide detailed information on how they use consumers’ data when they are setting prices. The commission said Wednesday it is also studying how ride-sharing and delivery companies like Uber use their independent drivers’ personal data when they are setting compensation rates. Orders were also issued to United, JetBlue, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart and Target. The FTC’s actions reflect customers’ increasing concerns about pricing technology and the use of artificial intelligence to collect vast amounts of data. Delta and JetBlue said Wednesday that they don't use personal data to set individualized prices.
headline: FTC orders Walmart, Delta and others to share how they use personal data to set prices and pay

author: MATTHEW LEE
description: Top diplomats from the Group of 20 largest world economies have wrapped up two days of talks in Atlanta but there's no consensus on several critical issues. Divisions, most notably over Russia’s war with Ukraine, overshadowed the start of the meeting and affected its outcome, too. As a result, the group didn't release a joint communique Saturday but relied on a chairman’s statement summarizing the talks that Secretary of State Marco Rubio released after the meetings closed. The statement made no mention of any agreements reached. It referred to priorities, from energy and food security to freedom of navigation, that G20 members determined were important to solve.
headline: G20 foreign ministers end Atlanta meeting without consensus on key issues

author: Sara Gregory
description: Under a public-private deal, the contractor will build and operate toll lanes on the eastern top of I-285 for 50 years.
headline: Georgia DOT picks team to build top-end I-285 toll lanes

author: Tamar Hallerman
description: Expect significant price hikes when Georgia Access open enrollment begins Nov. 1.
headline: Georgia won't allow ACA customers to preview plans before open enrollment

author: Rosie Manins
description: Georgia legislators are considering improvements to post-conviction litigation as the state's top judges warn of poor representation provided to some indigent defendants.
headline: ‘Beyond sad’: Georgia’s bad lawyering revealed in legislative study

author: Katherine Landergan
description: Georgia governor and attorney general candidates say more needs to be done to protect children in daycare and to address issues revealed in an AJC investigation.
headline: Georgia leaders, candidates say daycare injuries a major concern

author: Reed Williams
description: In a statement to the AJC, DeKalb County Sheriff Melody Maddox said the ordinance will subject unhoused people to arrest.
headline: Georgia county approves controversial 'urban camping' ordinance

author: Samantha Hogan
description: Georgia's daycare quality rating system is flawed with the state advertising hundreds of centers as quality daycares despite serious incidents of putting kids at risk.
headline: Children suffered burns and beatings. Georgia calls it quality daycare.

author: Nedra Rhone
description: Georgia’s Quality Rated program is meant to help parents find quality childcare, but ratings that fail to reflect serious safety problems can leave families in the dark.
headline: Nedra Rhone: Georgia daycare ratings must reflect child safety risks

author: Samantha Hogan
description: Six tips for how to compare Georgia daycares for licensing, child safety and ratings.
headline: Georgia childcare: How to background check a daycare

author: Katherine Landergan
description: Among the takeaways about daycares in Georgia is that state's quality rating system is flawed and daycares with serious safety violations have collected state money.
headline: 5 takeaways from the AJC’s daycare safety investigation

author: Adam Van Brimmer
description: A state judge decided the eligibility of a Georgia House candidate accused of voting in primary elections in both Nevada and Georgia earlier this year.
headline: Georgia House candidate accused of double voting gets a reprieve

author: Adam Van Brimmer
description: Georgia scales back a proposal allowing 1,500-foot-long docks to cross state-owned coastal marshland after public outcry, but a new rule would still allow wider docks.
headline: Georgia drops rule allowing 1,500-foot-long docks after opposition

author: Rosie Manins
description: A Southeast Georgia county and library system fired a library manager because she allowed a book about a transgender child to be displayed, her lawsuit alleges.
headline: Suit says transgender book got Georgia library manager fired

author: Charles Seabrook
description: Wildlife refuges put the needs of plants and animals first, unlike national parks. Here are 10 refuges you can visit in Georgia, including the Okefenokee Swamp.
headline: Georgia’s national wildlife refuges welcome visitors in October

author: Taylor Croft
description: Federal prosecutors say they indicted a Georgia businessman and Florida attorney on wire fraud, money laundering charges for allegedly defrauding investors out of $2 million.
headline: Georgia man charged in alleged $2M Ponzi schemes, feds say

author: Danny Robbins
description: Federal authorities have arrested two people accused of helping con artist Arthur Lee Cofield escape from prison. Their arrests could signify the first break in the case.
headline: 2 charged with helping Arthur Lee Cofield escape Georgia federal prison

author: Adam Van Brimmer
description: State agency to vote on allowing private residential docks up to 1,500 feet long and 6 feet wide on Georgia's coast amid public opposition.
headline: Georgia poised to allow 1,500-foot-long private docks on coast

author: BILL BARROW
description: Georgia Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is trying to make history as the first Black woman to be elected governor in the United States. Her bid carries all the more weight in a Deep South state where the former Atlanta mayor traces her family lineage to antebellum enslavement. She doesn't talk explicitly about her race. But some supporters see it shadowing Republican attacks of her tenure leading the city. Bottoms was mayor during the pandemic surge in crime and 2020 protests over police violence against Black men. Republican nominee Rick Jackson and President Donald Trump say Bottoms was a disaster. She calls that GOP frame an old line of attack.
headline: Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms navigates the challenges of Black women battling political barriers

author: Caroline Silva
description: The Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia will get a new restraint when the ride reopens. An Atlanta man was ejected from the popular coaster midride Oct. 12.
headline: Six Flags Over Georgia to add roller coaster seat belts after educator’s death

author: ALANNA DURKIN RICHER and ERIC TUCKER
description: The Justice Department has failed to secure a grand jury indictment against a former White House staffer who testified against President Donald Trump before a House committee investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, U.S. Capitol insurrection. Two people familiar with the matter said Tuesday the grand jury in Washington rejected prosecutors’ request to return an indictment charging Cassidy Hutchinson. It’s the latest setback in the Justice Department’s efforts to charge perceived adversaries of the Republican president. Hutchinson said Trump tried to let armed protesters avoid security screenings and grabbed at the steering wheel of the presidential SUV when the Secret Service refused to let him go to the Capitol. Trump calls Hutchinson a “total phony.”
headline: Grand jury refuses to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, AP sources say

author: Doug Turnbull
description: Officials recently approved a record-setting deal to build and collect on new I-285 toll lanes, but what about transit?
headline: I-285 express lanes draw criticism from some public transit supporters

author: PHILIP MARCELO
description: The New Jersey town that helped birth “The Addams Family” is embracing its ghoulish legacy. Westfield is the hometown of Charles Addams, the cartoonist who created the darkly eccentric, fictional family. Addams drew inspiration for his signature macabre style from the elegant Victorian homes, historic cemetery and other landmarks of the town just outside New York City. Every October, the town hosts AddamsFest with events that include an art exhibit, music festival, masquerade ball and other events. A self-guided heritage trail takes visitors past landmarks that informed Addams’ creations, including a Victorian-era house that helped inspire the fictional family's imposing, gothic abode.
headline: Hometown of ‘Addams Family’ creator becomes ghoulish Halloween destination

author: TIM SULLIVAN and NICHOLAS RICCARDI
description: Donald Trump roared back into office two years ago partly on the power of immigration. Trump’s pledge to seal the border and launch “mass deportations” earned him a wide swath of support, even in many heavily immigrant communities, amid frustration with the state of the border under former President Joe Biden. Nearly two years later, the public has soured on the president’s approach. More Americans now disapprove of Trump’s approach to immigration than approve of it, a striking turnaround that followed a nationwide crackdown that has seen thousands of working people detained, violent arrests caught on video and a string of deadly encounters with immigration officers, including the Minneapolis killings of two U.S. citizens.
headline: How Trump's immigration crackdown sparked a backlash that could boomerang in the midterms

author: THOMAS BEAUMONT and AAMER MADHANI
description: When President Donald Trump launched his war on Iran, he said it would last a matter of weeks. Now, eight months into it, rising energy costs and voter fatigue are weighing heavily on Republican candidates ahead of the midterm elections. An AP-NORC poll published last week found that voters from both major political parties want the next Congress to focus on making life more affordable and ending the war in Iran. But as the conflict grinds on, the situation in the Middle East has only become more complicated and is creating difficulties for Republicans making their case to voters.
headline: How Trump’s ‘little detour’ to Iran became a roadblock in the midterm elections

author: ERIC TUCKER, ALANNA DURKIN RICHER and MICHAEL KUNZELMAN
description: A federal judge has scolded the Justice Department for its unorthodox handling of a criminal case against two former FBI officials accused of making false statements to Congress about their participation in and knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden. U.S. Magistrate Zia Faruqui rejected an amended criminal complaint filed overnight by the Justice Department that added a new obstruction charge against the two former officials, Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides. Such charging documents require sign-off from a judge that probable cause exists that a crime was committed by a defendant. This complaint lacked that.
headline: Hunter Biden laptop issue resurfaces as judge scolds prosecutors over case against ex-FBI officials

author: ED WHITE
description: The Indiana Parole Board is recommending that the death penalty remain in place for a man who killed two children in a house fire. Jeffrey Weisheit has a right under Indiana law to ask for a life sentence for his 2013 murder and arson convictions. The final decision rests with Gov. Mike Braun. Weisheit's execution by lethal injection is scheduled for Nov. 5. Weisheit was convicted of setting a fire that killed his girlfriend's two children in Evansville in 2010.
headline: Indiana governor is urged to let death sentence proceed against man who killed 2 kids in fire

author: CHRISTOPHER RUGABER
description: The U.S. economy posted strong growth in the July-September quarter yet inflation remained stubbornly high last month, government reports showed Thursday, painting a mixed picture less than a week before midterm elections in which the uncomfortably high cost of living has become a central issue. Strong consumer spending and soaring investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure were the key drivers of growth in the third quarter. Whenever unemployment is low, like now, consumers often spend at a healthy clip, and wealthier consumers are increasingly spending the fruits of their stock market gains. Yet economists worry that persistently high prices are eroding Americans’ ability to keep spending.
headline: Strong growth and inflation paints mixed picture of economy days before midterm elections

author: JEFFREY COLLINS and KRISTIN M. HALL
description: The weekend escape of a Tennessee inmate who was convicted of murdering a co-worker was just the latest black eye for the state’s troubled prison system, coming only weeks after the failed execution of Christa Pike. Jacob Morley slipped through a fence at the Northwest Correctional Complex on Sunday. Authorities found a truck he stole abandoned in Marion, Illinois, on Tuesday, but they're trying to determine where he went from there. His escape highlights ongoing issues in Tennessee prisons, including understaffing and violence. After the failed execution of Pike last month, Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada announced his resignation. Critics say new leadership and transparency is needed.
headline: Inmate's escape is just the latest problem for Tennessee's troubled prison system

author: EDITH M. LEDERER
description: The head of the U.N. nuclear agency says there's been no indication Iran has tried to repair or reconstruct its nuclear facilities damaged in U.S. and Israeli military strikes this year or last year. During a U.N. Security Council meeting Tuesday, Rafael Grossi urged Iran to give inspectors access to all nuclear sites, including those damaged in the military attacks. Iran’s U.N. envoy lashed out at the U.S. and the council, never mentioning the unanswered questions or the demand for nuclear inspections. President Donald Trump says a major reason the U.S. went to war with Iran was to deny Tehran the ability to develop nuclear weapons, even as he insists strikes in June 2025 “obliterated” the country’s atomic program.
headline: Iran hasn't tried to repair nuclear facilities damaged in US strikes, UN nuclear chief says

author: JONATHAN LANDRUM Jr.
description: Jay-Z will headline the Super Bowl halftime show on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. The NFL, Apple Music, and Roc Nation announced the news Monday night. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he always wanted Jay-Z to perform when the time felt right. Jay-Z expressed excitement about the opportunity, calling it a dream come true. His Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to produce entertainment presentations, including the halftime show. Jay-Z, who has won 25 Grammy Awards, will perform at the stadium where he recently celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album, “Reasonable Doubt.”
headline: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show at SoFi Stadium in Southern California

author: FATIMA HUSSEIN
description: A federal judge has ruled that chronically ill people on Medicaid won’t be bound by new work requirement rules that the latest Trump administration guidance requires in order to qualify for “medically frail” exemptions. U.S. District Judge Richard Stearns in Boston gave a partial victory to a coalition of 25 states and the District of Columbia. They sued the Trump administration in June over the new Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services guidance tied to the 2025 law known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill.”
headline: Judge blocks Trump administration's Medicaid rule forcing sick recipients to prove frailty

author: SAFIYAH RIDDLE
description: A federal judge has rejected a Trump administration request to stop California from processing the ballots of up to 20,000 people. He warned it would “wreak havoc” on the midterm elections. Wednesday’s ruling by U.S. District Judge David O. Carter comes as more than 3.7 million people have already voted in the state. The decision is the latest legal setback for President Donald Trump in his efforts to expand federal control over state-run elections ahead of voting that will decide control of Congress for the rest of his term. The Republican administration sued election officials in the Democratic state in mid-October, accusing the officials of failing to meet a deadline to review 20,000 names it alleged were likely noncitizens on its voter rolls.
headline: Judge denies federal request to segregate California ballots, says it would 'wreak havoc' on voting

author: MICHAEL KUNZELMAN
description: A federal judge has agreed to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction that halts tree-cutting and other work at the East Potomac Golf Course. On Oct. 18, President Donald Trump announced plans on social media to close the golf course for 15 months and redevelop it despite a court challenge. Reyes previously ordered the administration to suspend work on the project until at least Oct. 26.
headline: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course in Washington

author: MICHAEL KUNZELMAN
description: A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to identify any state or local officials who received letters seeking their compliance with the government’s efforts to prevent non-U.S. citizens from voting in the midterm election. Chief Judge James Boasberg said he intends to rule by Monday — the eve of Election Day — on a request by Democratic Party leaders to block the Trump administration from attempting to undermine state election procedures next week. But the judge noted Thursday that the administration can render the case moot by filing a notice indicating that it will not engage in the election-related conduct the Democratic plaintiffs sued to challenge.
headline: Judge presses the Trump administration for details on its campaign to stop noncitizens from voting

author: ERIC TUCKER and MICHAEL KUNZELMAN
description: A federal judge has put off a decision on whether to dismiss a placeholder criminal case filed against former FBI Director James Comey, giving the Justice Department an opportunity to pursue an indictment over allegations of a decade-old news media leak. U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden acknowledged, though, that an indictment was no sure thing in a nation’s capital where grand juries have repeatedly rejected prosecutors’ requests for charges in politically delicate cases. He added that, in the meantime, he would be frustrated if there were some sort of pre-dawn raid to arrest Comey before he could be indicted, a concern defense attorneys raised.
headline: Judge puts off decision in Comey case as prosecutors pursue new indictment against ex-FBI head

author: GARY FIELDS
description: A federal judge says she'll open a “formal inquiry” to investigate if attorneys for the Trump administration violated ethics during a legal dispute about a golf-course project. It's one in a pair of plans that are revealing the breadth of the president’s attempts to mold parts of the District of Columbia as he wishes. The two cases, unfolding at the same time in the same federal courthouse, are also showing the underlying executive authority claims that lie beneath them. In turn, it's a glimpse into the uses of presidential power under Donald Trump. The cases involved are an impending shutdown and reconfiguration of a historic public golf course and the construction of a monumental arch.
headline: Judge wants to know if Trump attorneys violated ethics in one of 2 cases to change the DC landscape

author: ERIC TUCKER and ALANNA DURKIN RICHER
description: President Donald Trump’s Justice Department has been scrambling before the midterm election with a blitz of headline-making actions and cases that some critics say reeks of politics. This month alone, the Justice Department escalated an investigation into Democratic U.S. Rep. Ilhan Omar with a search of her home. It brought criminal charges against two former FBI officials accused of falsely downplaying their knowledge of investigations involving Hunter Biden. It revealed a fresh attempt to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey. And it made an unsuccessful attempt to indict a former White House aide who delivered dramatic but disputed testimony about Trump’s efforts to overturn the 2020 election.
headline: Trump's Justice Department pushes a spate of politically sensitive cases as midterm elections near

author: ALANNA DURKIN RICHER, JOSHUA GOODMAN and BECKY BOHRER
description: The U.S. Department of Justice is pushing for a court order to isolate certain Alaska ballots to investigate potential voter confusion, while federal officials confirmed the existence of a criminal probe over a Senate candidate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent. The dueling developments came days before Tuesday’s ranked choice general election, in a race headlined by two-term Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan and Democratic former U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola. The race is among a handful nationwide expected to determine control of the Senate. Peltola says she is not interested in “tricking voters.”
headline: Justice Department seeks to isolate Alaska ballots as criminal probe underway over Senate candidate

author: BILL BARROW
description: Kamala Harris has been campaigning for Democratic candidates across multiple states during the final stretch of the midterm elections. The former vice president is urging Black voters and others to channel their frustrations with President Donald Trump into ballot box decisions. She's considering whether to run for the White House in 2028, and her midterm itinerary took her to presidential battlegrounds and early primary states. But she also went to Mississippi and focused in all stops on core Democratic groups and policy ideas. She also used the tour to urge Democrats to be ruthless with power.
headline: Kamala Harris urges a 'too big to rig' turnout for the midterms and tees off on Trump

author: HILLEL ITALIE
description: Ken Burns has won a $250,000 prize for his contributions to American history. The New York Historical museum awarded him the inaugural David M. Rubenstein Prize for the Advancement of American History. The jury praised Burns for his work on topics like the American Revolution and the Civil War. They noted his films have brought the history of the U.S. to more people than perhaps any other single body of work. Burns expressed gratitude, acknowledging the collective effort of historians and archivists. The award was established earlier this year by financier David M. Rubenstein.
headline: Ken Burns wins a $250,000 prize for bringing American history to life

author: RUSS BYNUM
description: Five Spanish missionaries are being elevated one step away from sainthood nearly 430 years after they were killed in present-day Georgia. The Catholic Diocese of Savannah will hold a beatification ceremony Saturday for the five Franciscan friars. They were killed in 1597 by Indigenous people they had traveled to the New World to baptize, in what historical records say was a dispute over polygamy. Pope Francis decreed the missionaries as martyrs in 2025, capping decades of research and bureaucratic review. The diocese expects 10,000 people to attend the special Mass in Georgia.
headline: Killed almost 430 years ago, 5 Catholic friars will soon be one step from sainthood

author: Danny Robbins
description: Georgia med spas and wellness clinics are openly promoting and dispensing knockoff retatrutide, a drug still in clinical trials; state regulators haven’t stopped them.
headline: Unapproved weight loss drug openly sold in Georgia

author: BARBARA ORTUTAY
description: It reared its bony head in 2020, during that first, chaotic pandemic year that was rife with grief and fear but also toilet paper hoarding and questionable lockdown-inspired purchases. Behold Skelly, the 12-foot, 90-pound skeleton, on sale for $299 from Home Depot, just in time for Halloween — at least, if you can get your hands on one. Many did, because this is America. And when we get sad, stressed or bored, we shop, drowning our collective anxieties in things that we definitely don’t need but most certainly want.
headline: Make no bones about it, the giant skeleton has become an American Halloween fixture

author: MICHAEL R. SISAK
description: A state judge is considering whether social media posts by New York’s attorney general should disqualify her from leading a criminal investigation into gang rape allegations at Cornell University. The judge heard arguments Thursday. Attorney General Letitia James posted support online for the accuser days before taking over as special prosecutor in the case. One of the accused men argues the posts show James is biased. James’ office argues the challenge is meritless. The accuser is a former Cornell student. She filed a lawsuit last month alleging rape at a fraternity party in October 2024. The lawsuit led to the renewed criminal investigation.
headline: Man accused in Cornell rape lawsuit wants Letitia James removed from investigation over her posts

description: Authorities say a man serving a life sentence for murder has escaped from a prison in northwest Tennessee. Officials discovered 28-year-old Jacob Morley was missing late Sunday at the Northwest Correctional Complex. Security footage showed Morley going through a fence in his prison uniform. Prison officials didn't give additional details on how Morley made it through the fence. Law enforcement is searching buildings and other structures near the prison about 90 miles north of Memphis. Morley was convicted of killing his co-worker in 2022. The Northwest Correctional Complex has faced issues with violence and staffing shortages.
headline: Man serving a life sentence for murder slips through a fence and escapes a Tennessee prison

author: RONALD BLUM
description: Sandy Alcantara was blocked from becoming a free agent by the Miami Marlins, while Michael King went on the market and Bo Bichette decided to keep his contract with the New York Mets. Starting pitchers Sonny Gray and Nick Martinez also will become free agents after their teams declined mutual options. Miami exercised its $21 million option on Alcantara rather than pay a $2 million buyout, a decision that guarantees the pitcher $75 million over six years as part of the deal he agreed to in November 2021.
headline: Marlins exercise Alcantara option, King leaves Padres and Bichette stays with Mets

author: RONALD BLUM
description: Major League Baseball might face a long pause following the Milwaukee Brewers' first World Series title. Owners have proposed a salary cap, reminiscent of the 1994 plan that led to a 7 1/2-month strike. The current labor contract expires on Dec. 1, and a lockout us likely. This could spark a free-agent frenzy similar to 2021. Players and management remain divided on economic issues, with players opposing the cap and seeking expanded rights. Other major U.S. leagues have salary caps, but baseball players have consistently resisted such a system.
headline: MLB's 2027 season threatened with lockout looming when labor deal expires Dec. 1

author: Caroline Silva
description: Two women are charged with murder after a 4-year-old boy’s body was found under a pile of clothes at an Atlanta home, arrest warrants say.
headline: Warrants detail injuries, abuse of 4-year-old found dead in Atlanta

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: There should be no problem with the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream approaching the first WNBA Finals Game 7 in league history with a sense of urgency. Then again, that’s what Golden State coach Natalie Nakase thought about Game 6. She was baffled that her team somehow left behind its defensive intensity at the start of Thursday’s 80-69 loss to the Dream that forced Game 7 at “Ballhalla” in San Francisco on Saturday night. Nakase was still struggling to comprehend the lackadaisical start so she could make sure it’s not repeated in Saturday night’s decisive game.
headline: Nakase and Valkyries are determined to avoid another slow start in WNBA Finals Game 7 against Dream

author: The Associated Press
description: New Orleans and Atlanta play in non-conference action. The teams match up Saturday for the first time this season. New Orleans is 1-2 at home, and Atlanta is 2-1 on the road.
headline: New Orleans and Atlanta to meet in cross-conference matchup

author: The Associated Press
description: New York City FC and Atlanta United square off in Eastern Conference play.
headline: New York City FC hosts Atlanta United in Eastern Conference play

author: MARK LONG
description: No. 17 Florida is listing its top two quarterbacks, starter Aaron Philo and backup Tramell Jones Jr., as questionable to play Saturday against third-ranked Georgia in Atlanta. Philo and Jones have split repetitions in practice this week, and coach Jon Sumrall says the starting decision will come down to “health and availability.” Philo sat out a victory at then-No. 7 Texas on Oct. 17 because of an injured throwing shoulder. Jones stepped in and won his first career start, but he's been dealing with “a couple of bumps and bruises” since.
headline: No. 17 Florida lists QBs Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones as questionable for No. 3 Georgia

author: MARK LONG
description: No. 17 Florida will start quarterback Aaron Philo against third-ranked Georgia in the Southeastern Conference rivalry known as “The World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party." That's according to a person familiar with the decision. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because coach Jon Sumrall had not made his choice public. Philo and backup Tramell Jones Jr. were upgraded to probable on Friday for the game in Atlanta. They split repetitions in practice much of the week, and Sumrall said the decision would come down to “health and availability.”
headline: No. 17 Florida to start QB Aaron Philo against Georgia in the 'Cocktail Party,' AP source says

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: The World’s Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party will have a different feel when No. 3 Georgia plays No. 17 Florida in Atlanta for the first time. The usual neutral site setting of Jacksonville, Fla., is not available due to renovations at EverBank Stadium. Instead, the 50-50 split of tickets at Mercedes-Benz Stadium may provide a setting similar to the Southeastern Conference championship game held each year at the facility. The 2027 game will be played in Tampa Bay before the series returns to Jacksonville. Georgia is 8-2 in the rivalry with coach Kirby Smart, including wins in the last five games.
headline: No. 3 Georgia braces for test against No. 17 Florida as 'Outdoor Cocktail Party' moves to Atlanta

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: Chris Cole returned a fumble recovery 66 yards for a touchdown and No. 3 Georgia took advantage of four turnovers by No. 17 Florida to beat the Gators 27-8. Tramell Jones Jr., Florida’s second quarterback, fumbled when sacked by Quintavius Johnson late in the first half. Cole picked up the loose ball and scored on his second long fumble return of the season. Georgia enjoyed a strong recovery from its last-second 27-24 loss to Auburn on October 17. Aaron Philo was benched after throwing two interceptions in his return as Florida's starting quarterback.
headline: No. 3 Georgia takes advantage of 4 turnovers by No. 17 Florida to beat Gators 27-8

author: Shaddi Abusaid
description: Traffic has been rerouted since last Tuesday's bridge closure, causing heavier-than-usual delays in the area.
headline: No timeline for Moores Mill bridge reopening

author: Tamar Hallerman
description: This marks the second year with significant, double-digit increases as enrollment continues to fall.
headline: Georgia approves health insurance hikes of up to 29% for ACA plans

author: ALAN COLE
description: Onyeka Okongwu scored a season-high 29 points and had 12 rebounds, leading the Atlanta Hawks to a 114-111 victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Thursday night. Atlanta snapped a three-game losing streak to improve to 3-3, and halted Cleveland’s three-game winning streak. The Cavs are 3-2. Donovan Mitchell cut Atlanta’s lead to one on a driving layup with 20.6 seconds remaining. Nickeil Alexander-Walker made two free throws with 15.3 left to take the lead back to three and Mitchell got two potential tying looks off on the final possession, but misfired on both. James Harden led Cleveland with 24 points, followed by Mitchell with 22.
headline: Onyeka Okongwu has 29 points and 12 rebounds as Hawks beat Cavs 114-111 to snap skid

author: Adrianne Murchison
description: Terwilliger supported children’s health and medical research, housing initiatives and programs for veterans.
headline: Patricia Terwilliger, Atlanta political donor and philanthropist, dies at 83

author: MARK KENNEDY
description: Patrick Stewart, the classically trained stage actor who scaled the Shakespearean canon and added gravitas to a “Star Trek” franchise and the “X-Men” films, has died. He was 86. A spokesperson said Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia. Stewart was best known as Professor Charles Xavier from the “X-Men” and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” but he spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise.
headline: Patrick Stewart, legendary actor of ‘Star Trek’ and 'X-Men' fame, dies at 86

author: JOSH KELETY
description: Police in Georgia say three people, including two juveniles, have been arrested in connection with a plot to carry out a shooting at a high school in metro Atlanta. The three were arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to commit murder. Police say the FBI discovered threatening posts online from one of the trio and worked with local police to make the arrests on Oct. 20 and Oct. 23. Two were apprehended Georgia and the third in California. The announcement of the plot comes less than two weeks after a 16-year-old boy killed three children and a teacher in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in central Oregon.
headline: 3 people, including two minors, arrested in connection with a school shooting plot in metro Atlanta

description: A prominent Georgia Republican has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison for running a Ponzi scheme. Federal prosecutors say the scheme caused losses of over $76 million to more than 300 victims. Edwin Brant Frost IV pleaded guilty to wire fraud in May after an investigation that began when First Liberty Building and Loan collapsed in June 2025. Frost has publicly apologized and was ordered to pay restitution. Conservative talk shows often promoted investing in First Liberty. According to a lawsuit, Frost skimmed $17 million for himself and loaned millions more that were never repaid.
headline: Prominent Georgia Republican gets 15 years in prison after pleading guilty in Ponzi scheme

author: RONALD BLUM
description: The Tampa Bay Rays joined the Brooklyn Dodgers and Detroit Tigers as the only teams to lose in their first three World Series appearances. The Rays were beaten by the Milwaukee Brewers, who took the title for the first time by winning Game 5 by a 4-1 score. Manager Kevin Cash said the team is "banged up and hurting." Drew Rasmussen, who started on short rest, allowed one run and two hits over four innings. The Rays led the AL East from mid-May and topped the American League with 98 wins. Closer Bryan Baker said the team should use this as motivation to keep working.
headline: Rays become third team to lose first three World Series, joining Brooklyn Dodgers, Detroit Tigers

author: RONALD BLUM
description: Tampa Bay’s first World Series game at Tropicana Field in 18 years turned into a record-setter: for Milwaukee Brewers batters and Rays pitchers. Milwaukee became the first team to score eight runs with two outs in a World Series inning, running away with a 10-1 victory Monday night and a 3-0 lead in the best-of-seven series. Brewers batters strung together a postseason-record seven straight two-out hits against starter Freddy Peralta and relievers Cam Booser and Cole Sulser. Brice Turang, Garrett Mitchell and Cooper Pratt combined to drive in five runs in a three-pitch span, opening a 7-0 lead. Jackson Chourio had two hits in the inning, part of his four-hit night.
headline: Rays put on the brink of World Series flop by Brewers' historic 8-run, 2-out surge

author: RONALD BLUM
description: Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson singled home runs in a stunning 12th-inning rally, and the Tampa Bay Rays staved off World Series elimination with a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers that forced Game 5. Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th for his fourth hit of the night as Milwaukee neared a sweep and its first World Series title. But the Rays rallied in the bottom half after a throwing error by third baseman Joey Ortiz on Junior Caminero's leadoff grounder against reliever Antonio Senzatela. Liam Hicks singled off Shane Drohan, who relieved in his first appearance since Oct. 15, and DeLuca’s single to center drove in pinch-runner Cedric Mullins to tie the score at 3.
headline: Rays stun Brewers with 2-run rally in 12th inning and force World Series Game 5 with 4-3 win

author: BILL BARROW
description: Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico were making closing arguments Saturday in a tossup Texas U.S. Senate race that has become a key measure of voters’ frustration with Trump’s leadership and his loyalists in the Republican Party. Meanwhile in Michigan, Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed sought to shut down talk of the intraparty conflict with his primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens, calling it a distraction from issues that voters care about. The race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is another of this year’s most competitive contests, heightening Democratic fears. President Donald Trump took a break from daily rallies to talk to voters via telephone. He also attended a Halloween party at his Florida estate.
headline: Republicans on defense in Texas while Democrats in Michigan can't get on the same page

author: MATTHEW PERRONE
description: Food and Drug Administration staffers had little input on the Trump administration's decision that eases access to peptide drugs favored by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. That’s according to people familiar with the policy’s development who were interviewed by The Associated Press. The new policy was posted online Wednesday by Kennedy’s Department of Health and Human Services. It covers a handful of injectable peptides promoted within the wellness industry for uses such as building muscle, healing injuries and boosting energy. The policy directs the FDA not to take action against specialty pharmacies that sell a half-dozen wellness peptides.
headline: RFK Jr. eases access to unproven peptides despite opposition from FDA scientists

author: FATIMA HUSSEIN
description: Rising healthcare costs are a major concern for older Americans, and it's affecting their finances and political priorities. Open enrollment for Medicare began in October, with changes in costs and coverage. Prescription drug prices remain high and that's forcing some people to ration medications. Long-term care costs have also increased significantly. Social Security's future is uncertain, with potential benefit reductions by 2034 if funding issues aren't addressed. One 83-year-old retiree from Ohio says she faces financial strain due to medical expenses despite her careful retirement planning. Barbara Weigand recently withdrew $4,000 from her retirement account to cover cancer treatment costs.
headline: Rising health costs and coverage changes are big concerns for older adults as Election Day nears

author: Caroline Silva
description: More than 20 Salem High School students and staff were taken for medical treatment following a school bus crash. All have now been released from hospital.
headline: Salem High football players, staff involved in school bus crash

description: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the Trump administration did not help Flávio Bolsonaro leave Brazil after his election defeat. Bolsonaro arrived in Miami on Wednesday. The State Department said he and his family will be granted U.S. visas. Rubio told reporters in Atlanta that the U.S. government was not involved in Bolsonaro's move. Bolsonaro, who lost to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has refused to concede and claims the election was fraudulent. He is under investigation in Brazil for corruption and other charges. Bolsonaro calls himself a victim of persecution.
headline: Rubio says the US government did not facilitate Bolsonaro’s flight to the US

author: Tamar Hallerman
description: Medical providers from all over rural Georgia are reporting new strain since the beginning of the year — the result of major policy changes in Washington.
headline: Georgia’s rural healthcare under strain after thousands drop insurance

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: Georgia Tech has an almost completely revamped roster as it prepares to open its season under first-year coach Scott Cross. Cross, the former coach at Troy, is trying to build the Yellow Jackets' first winning season since 2019-20 with a roster that features no returning starters and only two returning lettermen. The Georgia Tech roster includes seven transfers and six freshmen. The Yellow Jackets finished 11-20 overall and 2-16 in the Atlantic Coast Conference last season. Kam Craft, who averaged 7.3 points last season, is the top returning scorer. The Yellow Jackets open the season on Tuesday against Hampton.
headline: Scott Cross faces almost complete roster overhaul as he takes over a rebuilding Georgia Tech program

author: MARY CLARE JALONICK
description: Get ready to fall back. The Senate is unlikely to act on a House-passed bill that would make daylight saving time permanent, despite pressure from President Donald Trump and Americans who don’t like having to change their clocks twice a year. Daylight saving time ends early Sunday, requiring much of the U.S. to move clocks back one hour. Several senators are holding up legislation that would eliminate that longtime U.S. tradition. Supporters argue that ending the time change would provide more daylight during the times Americans are most active. Opponents say commuters in some states wouldn’t see the sun until after 9 a.m.
headline: Senate is skeptical about making daylight saving time permanent despite Trump's pressure

author: MICHAEL KUNZELMAN
description: A federal judge has set a September 2027 trial date for a man charged with attempting to kill President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner. Cole Tomas Allen’s trial is scheduled to start with jury selection on Sept. 7 and is expected to last approximately three to four weeks. Prosecutors had recommended starting the trial in May 2027, but U.S. District Judge Trevor McFadden set the later date on Thursday after Allen’s attorneys asked for more time to prepare. Allen is accused of storming the WHCA dinner and firing a shotgun at a Secret Service officer who tried to stop the April 25, 2026, attack.
headline: September 2027 trial date set for man charged with attacking White House correspondents’ dinner

author: JESSE BEDAYN
description: Cindy Banda faces mounting medical bills after battling breast cancer. Despite the single mother's positive outlook, the financial strain combined with the high cost of living is overwhelming. And it's made the Texan who's a three-time supporter of President Donald Trump rethink her politics. Rising healthcare costs are a major concern for many in the United States heading into the Nov. 3 election. Polling shows that registered voters tend to trust Democrats more than Republicans to handle healthcare. Banda knows how that feels. And for the first time in her life she's voted Democratic, casting an early ballot for James Talarico, in the U.S. Senate race.
headline: She voted for Trump every time. Then came cancer and the bills

author: The Associated Press
description: A shooting at a Spirit Halloween store in California on the eve of the holiday has left a pregnant woman dead and six other people wounded. Police say gunfire erupted inside the store at the Solano Town Center in Fairfield late Friday. All seven victims suffered gunshot wounds. One died, and three were in critical condition. No arrests have been made. Detectives are investigating and speaking with witnesses to try to identify a suspect. Fairfield is a city of about 120,000 residents southwest of Sacramento.
headline: Shooting at Spirit Halloween store in California leaves pregnant woman dead and 6 wounded

author: Rebecca McCarthy
description: Shouky Saheen become a successful Atlanta businessman and philanthropist. Born in Chicago, he died of cancer on Oct. 4 at his Atlanta home.
headline: Atlanta businessman, philanthropist Shouky Shaheen dies at 97

author: Shaddi Abusaid
description: The Goliath roller coaster will remain closed as Six Flags Over Georgia reopens for the first time since Monday's deadly incident.
headline: Cobb amusement park to reopen as roller coaster death investigation continues

author: Caroline Silva
description: An escort ad led Kingston Bradley to contact the woman whose remains were found last month at his Cobb County apartment complex, according to court testimony Friday.
headline: Detective: Photo of woman's body found on phone of teen charged in Smyrna dismemberment

author: Rosie Manins
description: The Maynards (plantiffs) allege that Christal McGee told her three passengers right before the crash that she was trying to hit 100 mph, to post it on Snapchat.
headline: Snapchat settles lawsuit over the app's discontinued speed filter

author: Caroline Silva
description: An Atlanta social media celebrity with millions of followers was federally indicted for fraudulently obtaining more than $4 million in SNAP benefits, authorities say.
headline: Social media celeb who paraded luxury life indicted in alleged Georgia SNAP fraud

author: The Associated Press
description: If you love sports, it's tough to beat Monday night. Five professional leagues in North America were in action at the same time, a phenomenon known as a sports equinox. Major League Baseball and the NFL are competing for the most viewers while the NBA, WNBA and NHL give their diehard fans games to watch. Sportradar says Monday marked the 33rd sports equinox, the first since Oct. 27, 2025 and the fourth instance with women’s professional basketball included in the sports smorgasbord.
headline: Sports equinox features MLB, NFL, NBA, WNBA and NHL all playing at the same time Monday night

author: NICHOLAS RICCARDI and ALI SWENSON
description: President Donald Trump's involvement in this year's midterm elections has moved from rhetoric to reality. The president directed his administration to intervene on behalf of his preferred candidate in Alaska's Senate race, suing to halt the certification before voters have even finished casting ballots. And then on Thursday, his Department of Justice issued election-related subpoenas in Alaska and California. Trump has long told supporters that elections he or his party might lose are stolen, and this year is no exception. But the lawsuits and subpoenas elevate Trump’s crusade beyond rhetoric.
headline: Stolen election rhetoric from Trump isn't new. His ability to act on those claims is

author: Asia Simone Burns
description: Top Georgia officials and weather authorities across the state are urging people to take precautions as they continue to monitor the impacts of Hurricane Isaias.
headline: Hurricane Isaias brings heavy rain, strong winds, power outages to Georgia

author: KATE BRUMBACK
description: Authorities say that the suspects in an alleged plot to carry out a shooting at a Georgia high school had a floor plan of the school and had chosen a date. Police accused 17-year-old Shane Keith Taylor and 21-year-old Michael Brandon Terry, along with an unidentified juvenile, of planning a shooting at Cherokee High School. The FBI identified threatening social media posts and notified school police, who contacted the Canton Police Department. Police arrested the juvenile suspect on October 20, and Taylor and Terry on October 23. Investigators collected guns, ammunition, and electronic devices as evidence. The investigation remains active.
headline: Suspects in alleged school shooting plot in Georgia had floor plan, had chosen a date, warrants say

author: AJC Communications
description: Podcast with the Pulitzer Center examines how Georgia became the epicenter of the fight over election administration, public trust and democracy.
headline: ‘The Final Tally,’ a three-part podcast on election integrity, debuts

author: The Associated Press
description: The Justice Department has issued subpoenas to California officials in an escalation of its scrutiny of local election administration. According to a person familiar with the matter who insisted on anonymity to discuss an ongoing investigation, the subpoenas were being issued by all four U.S. attorneys in California. The move follows a federal judge’s appointment of a special master earlier Thursday to evaluate claims that California has about 20,000 noncitizens on its voter rolls. The Justice Department also is escalating a criminal investigation over an Alaska Senate candidate who shares a name with the Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan, issuing a raft of new grand jury subpoenas, a person familiar with the matter told The Associated Press on Thursday.
headline: The Latest: DOJ subpoenas California officials in escalation of local election scrutiny

author: The Associated Press
description: The top federal prosecutor in Alaska is confirming the existence of a criminal investigation related to an alleged scheme to confuse voters by putting a Senate candidate on the ballot with the same name as the Republican incumbent, Sen. Dan Sullivan. The department also confirmed Friday in court documents that it is seeking to isolate ballots ranking Dan J. Sullivan to probe “confusion.” The move comes after revelations earlier this week from The New York Times that Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola’s campaign appeared to be involved in recruiting Dan J. Sullivan. Peltola has denied that she knew anything about an effort to put the candidate on the Alaska ballot.
headline: The Latest: Justice Department looks to separate Alaska ballots that rank Dan J. Sullivan

author: MICHAEL CASEY
description: A former Massachusetts police detective is being tried on charges that he killed a pregnant woman to hide that he had begun sexually abusing her when she was 15. Matthew Farwell is accused of strangling Sandra Birchmore in 2021. An initial police investigation quickly concluded that Birchmore's death was a suicide. But the FBI began looking into the case two years later. Security camera footage places Farwell at Birchmore's home the night she died. Investigators recovered 40,000 texts between the two. Farwell's lawyers acknowledge that the married detective had an affair with Birchmore but say he did not kill her.
headline: The police said Sandra Birchmore's death was a suicide. Then the FBI accused a cop of murder

author: CHRISTINE BENZ of Morningstar
description: This common healthcare cost can catch retirees off guard, and Medicare offers little protection. Here’s how to plan for it.
headline: The retirement expense you may be missing

author: LAURA UNGAR
description: For the first time in a dozen years, a leading OB-GYN group has updated its guidance on managing hot flashes, night sweats, sleep changes and other disruptive symptoms that often come along with menopause. Menopause occurs when a woman has gone 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period, and happens around age 50 in the U.S. Doctors stressed the importance of hormone therapies, which many women are considering again after the removal of federal safety warnings. The American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists also described various nonhormonal options in the new advice released this month.
headline: There's new guidance on menopause symptoms like hot flashes. What women need to know

author: Rodney Ho
description: Tom Houck, former driver for Martlin Luther King Jr., civil rights activist, political consultant and media pundit, has died at age 79.
headline: Tom Houck, raconteur, civil rights activist and former driver for MLK, dies at 79

author: JEFFREY COLLINS
description: Authorities say an escaped Tennessee inmate convicted of murdering a co-worker stole a truck from a nearby farm and apparently made it to southern Illinois before abandoning it. Jacob Morley, who was serving a life sentence for killing a co-worker four years ago, was found to be missing from the Northwest Correctional Complex late on Sunday. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation says Morley stole a farm truck about 2 miles from the prison at about 1 a.m. Monday. Investigators say the truck was found abandoned Tuesday in Marion, Illinois, about 120 miles north of the prison. The police chief in Marion says no other stolen vehicles or suspicious things have been reported in his city.
headline: Truck stolen by escaped Tennessee inmate is found abandoned in Illinois, authorities say

author: MICHELLE L. PRICE, SEUNG MIN KIM and JOEY CAPPELLETTI
description: President Donald Trump rallied with Republican supporters in Florida on Friday while former President Bill Clinton spoke to Democrats just two states over in Mississippi. Both of them beseeched voters to head to the polls for the midterm election that will determine which party controls Congress. As early voting surges, Trump reshuffled his weekend schedule to rally Republicans in two states with critical Senate races: Iowa and Kansas. He had canceled plans to return to the states, only to rebook the events for Sunday. The about-face underscores his party’s push to drive turnout before Election Day.
headline: Trump and Clinton rally as early voting surges, Alaska probe widens, and Michigan Democrats feud

author: WILL WEISSERT
description: President Donald Trump wants midterm voters to imagine he's on the ballot and has seized the political spotlight in a way that makes such make-believe seem a bit more real. He's making 30-plus campaign stops around the country with low approval ratings, and he organized a pre-midterm convention in Dallas and used taxpayer-funded ads to promote himself. Trump believes injecting himself into races whenever possible is the best way to win. His strategy has sometimes backfired, as during the 2018 midterms. This time, polls suggest more voters disapprove of Trump than support him. Democrats are therefore betting on a backlash, and have spent heavily on advertising focusing on Trump and his administration's policies.
headline: Trump's cure for Republicans' midterm woes is more Trump. Will it work?

author: CARA ANNA
description: Lana Nusseibeh, a diplomat from the United Arab Emirates, is the newest contender for United Nations secretary-general. She brings Palestinian roots and defense of UAE-Israel relations to her candidacy to lead the world body. But she faces criticism over her country's alleged support for paramilitary fighters in Sudan's civil war, which the UAE denies. Any leader succeeding Antonio Guterres in January would inherit a U.N. weakened by harsh criticism and steep funding cuts by the Trump administration.  Nusseibeh aims to rebuild trust in the U.N. and promote “quiet diplomacy.” She has been outspoken on issues like aid for Gaza and women's roles internationally.
headline: UAE diplomat running for UN chief faces questions on her country's alleged support for Sudan rebels

author: FARNOUSH AMIRI
description: The U.N. General Assembly has condemned the U.S. economic embargo of Cuba for the 34th year. It comes even as Washington’s campaign to influence the outcome led to a number of countries voting against the resolution or sitting out the decision for the first time. The vote on Wednesday was 130-17, with 25 abstentions. The vote last year was 165-7, with 12 abstentions. Western countries like Germany, Italy and Latvia are among those that abstained for the first time in 34 years.
headline: UN condemns US economic embargo of Cuba though more nations sit out after Trump administration push

author: BEN FINLEY
description: The U.S. military says it has attacked a boat it accused of smuggling drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean. Tuesday's attack killed five people. It brings the number of people who have been killed by the U.S. military's boat strikes to at least 240. The Trump administration began targeting those it calls “narcoterrorists” in September 2025. President Donald Trump has said the U.S. is in an “armed conflict” with drug cartels in Latin America. He has sought to justify the attacks by saying they stem the flow of drugs into the U.S. But critics have questioned the overall legality of the boat strikes as well as their effectiveness.
headline: US military says 5 were killed by a strike on an alleged drug boat in the eastern Pacific

author: AAMER MADHANI and SAMY MAGDY
description: U.S. officials have warned Middle East allies to prepare for potential renewed military action against Iran after the U.S. midterm elections. That's according to two diplomats familiar with the matter who were not authorized to comment publicly and spoke on the condition of anonymity. President Donald Trump has not made a final decision but has suggested action could follow the elections. Regional officials were also warned to be on alert for potential retaliation from Iran and its proxies. The Pentagon recently deployed additional troops and ships to the Persian Gulf.
