They are expected to arrive in the region soon after Election Day in the United States.
headline: US warns allies to prepare for possible Iran strikes, retaliation after elections, AP sources say

author: Jessica Ryan, Sonja Sutcavage and Parker McCollum
description: Inhumane conditions have led to suffering, death at Valdosta State Prison, Southern Center for Human Rights law group alleges in report.
headline: South Georgia prison conditions create humanitarian crisis, group says

description: Volkswagen has posted a $6.5 billion after-tax loss for the July-September quarter. The company faces challenges like weak demand in China, U.S. tariffs, and lower profits from electric vehicles. The results, announced Thursday, highlight the need for cost-cutting measures, which could lead to the loss of up to 100,000 jobs and the closure of four German plants. Sales revenue decreased by 6.3% to 80.3 billion euros. Earnings also suffered from a 6.4 billion euro reduction in the value of Volkswagen's stake in Porsche. The company is under pressure to act quickly and decisively.
headline: Volkswagen posts $6.5 billion quarterly loss as China slump, Porsche writedown weigh on bottom line

author: Rosie Manins
description: Yamaha and Honda are liable for a Georgia man's aggressive cancer caused by asbestos exposure, a DeKalb County jury has found, awarding him $5 million.
headline: Georgia man wins $5M at trial against Yamaha, Honda

author: STEVE MEGARGEE
description: Like so many Milwaukee fans, Christian Yelich took a moment while celebrating the Brewers’ first World Series title to remember a man he wished had been around to see it. Yelich said he knew beloved broadcaster Bob Uecker was smiling somewhere after the Brewers' 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 5 of the World Series. Uecker died in January 2025 at the age of 90. Yelich had developed a close friendship with Uecker while emerging as the face of the Brewers' franchise. The Brewers announced last month they had made Yelich the first team captain in franchise history.
headline: Yelich pays tribute to Uecker after finally leading Brewers to their first World Series title

author: JESSICA DAMIANO
description: Looking for the perfect holiday gift for the gardener in your life? Vita’s Urbana Keyhole Composting Garden combines a vegetable garden and a composter in one. Your kitchen scraps will decompose naturally to nourish the surrounding plants. Or for digging in tight spaces, you might try Sneeboer’s Great Dixter Planting Spade. Cocktail lovers can toast last season's tomatoes with a glass of Crop Tomato Organic Vodka. Treleaf trellises add style to climbing plants. And the Birdfy Bath Pro birdbath streams live video to your phone. Parakito wristbands offer mosquito protection. And the LeafyPod uses AI to help care for houseplants.
headline: 8 gardening and garden-themed gifts for the holidays, from tools to smart tech

author: AJ Willingham
description: Morning, y’all. Your Nov. 2 update: Election concerns, a historic mass in Savannah, Bert Weiss discusses life after "The Bert Show" and more.
headline: A.M. ATL: Lock in

author: LAURA UNGAR
description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a generic version of the world’s only twice-a-year shot to prevent HIV. This is a big step toward making the extremely effective drug available inexpensively and quickly in 120 low- and middle-income countries. The drug, called lenacapavir, is expected to cost $40 a person each year in these places, the same price as daily preventive pills available now. But the shots are much more convenient than the pills because they’re needed much less frequently. The generic will not be available in the U.S. because there is a brand-name version still protected by a patent.
headline: Approval of a cheap version of HIV-prevention shot lenacapavir raises hopes in low-income countries

description: Miguel Almiron and Alexey Miranchuk each had a goal and an assist, Cooper Sanchez also scored and Atlanta United beat Toronto FC 3-1. Atlanta (9-18-6) ended a six-game winless run at home. Toronto (9-12-12), which had earned points in four of its last five MLS matches, was eliminated from playoff contention for the sixth straight season. Almiron opened the scoring in the 22nd minute. He played a give-and-go with Miranchuk before poking it through the legs of goalkeeper Luka Gavran. Sanchez gave Atlanta a 2-0 lead in the 40th. Almiron was left wide open along the left sideline, and he dribbled it along the end line before finding an unmarked Sanchez near the spot for a one-touch finish. Miranchuk made it 3-0 in the 51st by cleaning up a rebound.
headline: Atlanta United eliminates Toronto FC from playoff contention with 3-1 victory

description: Retired managers Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, Joe Maddon and Lou Piniella are on the Hall of Fame's contemporary era committee ballot for managers, executives and umpires. The committee meets Dec. 6 at the winter meetings in San Diego. Former general managers Sandy Alderson and Brian Sabean are on the ballot along with the late Atlanta Braves owner Ted Turner and former player, broadcaster and National League president Bill White. The 16 voters' identities will be revealed closer to the meeting, and 75% of the vote is needed for election. Inductees will be honored next July along with players voted in by the Baseball Writers’ Association of America.
headline: Baker, Bochy, Maddon and Piniella among 8 men on Hall of Fame contemporary era committee ballot

author: RONALD BLUM
description: New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams. Milwaukee first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers along with Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon. A player has until Nov. 17 to accept. Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 prior offers have been accepted. The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year.
headline: Bednar, Suzuki and Arozarena are among 8 MLB players receiving $23.15 million qualifying offers

author: ROB MAADDI
description: Baker Mayfield didn’t complete a pass but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers beat the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 on Sunday behind Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell’s rushing on a wet, sloppy field. The Buccaneers set a team record for yards rushing in a game with 324, and became the first team to have zero completions since Buffalo on Sept. 29, 1974. Irving ran for 170 yards and a touchdown on 27 carries, Gainwell ran for 140 on 25 carries and Chase McLaughlin kicked three field goals to stay perfect this season. Mayfield was 0 for 3 passing. Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions.
headline: Buccaneers beat Falcons 16-0 despite failing to complete a single pass in wet, sloppy conditions

description: Christian Walker of Houston and Matt Olson of Atlanta have each won their fourth Gold Gloves. Boston's Wilyer Abreu won his third consecutive fielding honor. The Red Sox and Arizona Diamondbacks led with three winners each. Boston's Ceddanne Rafaela and Arizona's Gabriel Moreno were among the repeat winners. First-time winners included Arizona's Geraldo Perdomo and Corbin Carroll. Other notable winners were Alex Bregman of the Chicago Cubs and the New York Yankees' Cody Bellinger. Voting involved managers and coaches, with a defensive index from the Society for American Baseball Research contributing to the results.
headline: Christian Walker, Matt Olson win 4th Gold Gloves and Wilyer Abreu gets his 3rd

description: Attorneys jousted at the Idaho Supreme Court over whether Lori Vallow Daybell’s convictions for killing her two youngest children and conspiring to murder a romantic rival should be thrown out. She claims she wasn’t allowed to have the lawyer she wanted at her 2023 trial. She is asking Idaho’s highest court to reverse her convictions in the deaths of Joshua “JJ” Vallow, Tylee Ryan and Tammy Daybell, whose husband married Vallow Daybell weeks later. Vallow Daybell was later convicted in Arizona for conspiring to murder her former husband and her niece’s ex-husband, the latter of whom survived.
headline: Court hears Lori Vallow Daybell's appeal over killings of her 2 youngest children, romantic rival

author: DAVE SKRETTA
description: The college basketball season tips off with many players unexpectedly gaining an extra year of eligibility. They have received injunctions from courts in various states after the NCAA adopted a new five-year eligibility model that did not apply to them as they wrapped up their playing careers last season. As of last week, the NCAA reported about 200 lawsuits involving 850 athletes. So far, most of the courts — though not all — have sided with athletes seeking another year of eligibility. But nothing has been definitively decided as the season gets underway, leaving coaches to wonder whether their players will remain eligible through March.
headline: Courtroom chaos hits college basketball as dozens play after judges block NCAA eligibility rules

author: Taylor Croft
description: Two DeKalb County police officers were shot and injured Sunday night while responding to a domestic incident, officials say.
headline: 2 DeKalb officers shot while responding to domestic incident

author: CYBELE MAYES-OSTERMAN
description: The former head of the FBI's Chicago field office has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration, accusing it of pushing him out after he was wrongly blamed for a failed felony prosecution. In the suit filed Monday, Douglas DePodesta accused Andrew Boutros, the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, of telling superiors he was to blame for a failed prosecution of six people who protested at an immigration enforcement facility in a Chicago suburb last fall. Boutros dropped all charges against them in May. Boutros’ office declined to comment. The FBI and Justice Department did not immediately return a request for comment.
headline: Ex-Chicago FBI chief says he was ousted over a failed protesters case, sues Justice Department

author: FRED GOODALL
description: Michael Penix Jr. had the worst performance of his NFL career while playing near his hometown. The Atlanta Falcons quarterback threw four interceptions in rainy conditions in a 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. His Bucs counterpart, Baker Mayfield, attempted only three passes and completed none. Penix refused to use the weather as an excuse. He grew up in Dade City, Florida, and attended high school in Tampa. He says it's “tough” to have a performance like that with relatives in the stands. The Falcons fell to 3-5 — including 3-3 since Penix returned from an injury he suffered last season.
headline: Falcons' Michael Penix Jr. vows to bounce back from worst performance of his young career

author: MICHELLE L. PRICE, SEUNG MIN KIM and MORIAH BALINGIT
description: President Donald Trump stood silently while triumphant music played as he held up a poster showing an image of the algae-clogged pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial. It was the final moment of his last big speech before Election Day, far away from the campaign trail where Republicans were trying Monday to make their case to voters to hang onto control of Congress. The president’s decision to spend the day before the pivotal midterms showing off his renovations in the nation’s capital instead of barnstorming around the country was a puzzling way to pitch America on keeping his party in power. He said he has more such major projects to come.
headline: Far from the campaign trail, Trump promotes his Reflecting Pool makeover before Election Day

author: MICHAEL CASEY
description: A federal judge has dismissed a lawsuit against Harvard University over its alleged failure to provide admissions records that the Justice Department demanded to ensure the Ivy League school stopped using affirmative action in admissions. The Justice Department said Harvard thwarted its efforts to investigate potential discrimination. The department accused Harvard of refusing to comply with a federal investigation and asked a judge to order the university to turn over the records. But U.S. District Judge Myong Joun concluded the department didn't take the necessary procedural steps to get the data before filing the lawsuit.
headline: Federal judge dismisses lawsuit against Harvard over federal demand for admissions data

author: PHILIP MARCELO, MICHAEL CASEY and CHRISTOPHER WEBER
description: Heavy rains and flash flooding have prompted mandatory evacuation orders in parts of the U.S. Southwest. In Colorado, officials in Pagosa Springs warned Sunday of potentially catastrophic flooding as the San Juan River was forecast to crest at more than 19 feet Sunday night. Officials say anyone in low-lying areas along the San Juan, Rio Blanco, Navajo, and Piedra rivers should head to a designated shelter at a local church. Officials in Sedona, Arizona, ordered residents in areas near Oak Creek to leave immediately as floodwaters were rising rapidly and multiple people were already trapped in their homes.
headline: Flash flooding triggers evacuations in Southwest and dire warning for Colorado spa town

author: CHRISTOPHER WEBER and RUSS BYNUM
description: A massive amount of water from unusually heavy rains is flowing through flood-weary parts of the Southwest. Over 20 trillion gallons of water has fallen on the Four Corners states and Nevada in the past two weeks, according to calculations by former National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration chief scientist Ryan Maue. The flooding is forcing evacuations and keeping swift-water rescue teams busy. One person died after falling into floodwaters in Flagstaff, Arizona, and police suspect a second death also is weather-related. The National Weather Service estimates as much as 4 more inches of rain could fall across the Four Corners region through Monday.
headline: Floods swamp the arid Southwest, forcing evacuations and altering Election Day plans

author: MARK LONG
description: Florida’s nearly 40-year scoring streak almost came to an end against Southeastern Conference rival Georgia on Saturday. The Gators needed to convert two fourth-down plays on a fourth-quarter drive to extend their NCAA-record streak to 481 games. TCU holds the second-longest streak at 427 consecutive games. Tramell Jones Jr.'s keeper on put the Gators on the scoreboard with 6:59 to play in a 27-8 loss in Atlanta. The touchdown prevented the relocated “Cocktail Party” from becoming a shutout celebration for the Bulldogs.
headline: Florida's late TD avoids a shutout and extends NCAA-record scoring streak to 481 games

author: Jim Halley
description: Five Franciscan missionaries killed in 1597 along what is today Georgia's coast moved closer to Catholic sainthood Saturday at a beatification ceremony in Savannah.
headline: Georgia Martyrs move closer to sainthood in beatification ceremony

author: Doug Turnbull
description: Commercials and movies glamorize holding a throttle wide open on the public roads, but drivers could use more cultural nudges to slow down.
headline: Drivers need more cultural nudges to slow down on busy roads

description: Atlanta Hawks guard Kingston Flemings was suspended for a game without pay by the NBA on Sunday night for intentionally elbowing New Orleans Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head. Flemings was assessed a technical foul and ejected with 3:04 remaining in the Hawks’ 121-99 road loss Saturday night. Flemings will sit out Monday night at Indiana.
headline: Hawks' Flemings suspended for a game for elbowing the Pelicans' McGowens in the head

author: Taylor Croft
description: A former High Museum of Art executive was sentenced to 12 months in prison in federal court Monday after stealing over $600,000 from the museum.
headline: Former High Museum exec gets 1 year in prison for $600K embezzlement

author: EDITH M. LEDERER
description: The president of the International Criminal Court has accused the Trump administration of trying to obstruct international justice by imposing penalties on the tribunal and has vowed that it would not succeed. Judge Tomoko Akane of Japan gave a remote briefing Monday at the United Nations because she faces U.S. sanctions. She called on all 193 U.N. member nations to act in defense of the court. The Trump administration has imposed a series of sanctions on ICC officials and then targeted the entire court last month as part of its campaign to dismantle the tribunal over investigations into the United States and its allies, including Israel.
headline: ICC president hits back at Trump administration penalties in remote UN address

author: ANNA WILDER and JACK BROOK
description: A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer who's accused of intentionally ramming his car into a Mexican construction worker in Houston has turned himself in. Mario Alberto Morales made his first court appearance Monday on a felony charge of aggravated assault with a deadly weapon for striking Miguel Parra Hernandez with an unmarked SUV on Oct. 10. Morales was chasing the 48-year-old construction worker through a parking lot. A grand jury indicted the 33-year-old Morales on Friday. His attorney has said he did not commit a crime. A judge sent bond at $30,000.
headline: ICE officer accused of hitting immigrant in Houston with an SUV turns himself in

author: ED WHITE
description: Indiana’s governor turned down a clemency request and says an execution planned for Thursday will go forward against a man who killed his girlfriend’s two children in 2010. Gov. Mike Braun said Monday he accepted the Indiana Parole Board’s recommendation to let the death sentence stand against Jeffrey Weisheit. The 50-year-old had a right to ask Braun to reduce the death sentence to a life sentence. Two children died in a house fire in the Evansville area 16 years ago. Their mother was at work at the time. Her relationship with Weisheit was breaking down.
headline: Indiana governor says execution will go ahead Thursday against man who killed 2 kids

author: ADITHI RAMAKRISHNAN
description: A chaotic climate phenomenon called El Niño is intensifying heavy rains and floods in the Southwest. Experts say the natural warming cycle is sizzling Pacific Ocean waters and leaking moisture into the air that can fuel passing storms. The phenomenon wasn’t the only cause, but scientists say it’s making heavy rains more likely and intense across the Southern U.S. Flash floods on Sunday prompted evacuations across northern New Mexico and central Arizona, and a Colorado ski town braced for its main river to rise to catastrophic levels. To stay safe, experts recommended watching the forecast, planning ahead and heeding evacuation warnings.
headline: Is El Niño making storms and flash floods in the Southwest worse?

description: Infielder Teruaki Sato of the Central League’s Hanshin Tigers and right-handers Kaima Taira of the  Saitama Seibu Lions and Hiromi Itoh of the Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters in the Pacific League are entering Major League Baseball’s posting system and will be available to teams to sign as a free agent from Monday until Dec. 16. Infielder Si-Hwan Roh of South Korea’s Hanwha Eagles is entering the posting system and can sign as a free agent from until Dec. 1. Sato, a left-handed-hitting 27-year-old third baseman and occasional outfielder, hit .306 with 39 homers and 106 RBIs, winning the Central League’s Triple Crown.
headline: Japanese players Teruaki Sato, Kaima Taira and Hiromi Itoh enter MLB posting system

author: AMY TAXIN
description: U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says all nine people died aboard a business jet that crashed into a Florida neighborhood. The aircraft departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas. Duffy said Sunday that the Federal Aviation Administration is sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation into the crash. The Learjet 60 carrying nine people nose-dived into a South Florida neighborhood Sunday and erupted into a giant fireball that appeared to just miss homes near a busy roadway, creating a giant fiery crater in the pavement.
headline: Jet nosedives and erupts into fireball near busy roadway in South Florida. All 9 on board died

author: ERIC TUCKER
description: A federal judge in Washington has dismissed a criminal complaint against two former FBI officials accused of lying to Congress about Hunter Biden, citing what he calls “weaponization” of President Donald Trump's Justice Department. The judge Monday said the investigation that produced the charges was overtly political. The Justice Department may still have an opportunity to pursue a grand jury indictment against the ex-FBI officials. The case accused the former officials of misleading Congress about their knowledge of efforts to investigate a laptop the Justice Department says was dropped off by Joe Biden’s son at a Delaware computer repair shop in 2019. The case sought to echo grievances by Trump and his Republican allies.
headline: Judge cites 'weaponization' in tossing charges for ex-FBI agents accused of lying about Hunter Biden

author: NICHOLAS RICCARDI and BECKY BOHRER
description: A federal judge has dismissed a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska’s U.S. Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses. The race is among the country’s most closely watched and is among a handful that is expected to determine control of the chamber. Sullivan’s main challenger in Tuesday’s ranked-choice general election is Democratic former U.S. Rep. Mary Peltola. The race includes two other candidates who have done almost no campaigning, one of whom shares the incumbent’s name. The lawsuit called for an investigation into whether votes cast for the other Sullivan were intended for the senator. Attorneys for the state and Peltola said the lawsuit lacked any legal basis.
headline: Judge dismisses lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska Senate race if GOP incumbent loses

author: NICHOLAS RICCARDI
description: The Justice Department is urging a federal judge to consider whether to hold an immigrant rights group in contempt of court for disclosing the results of its analysis of a dataset of alleged noncitizens registered to vote in California. The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights and its lawyers on Saturday filed documents in a legal case challenging the Trump administration's use of the data to target voters. Its analysis found more than 40% of the names on the administration's list were not on California's voter rolls. The administration says that's a possible violation of restrictions the judge put on access to the list and called for sanctions in court papers filed Sunday.
headline: Justice Department urges sanctions for database analysis critical of its noncitizen voting claims

author: JAMIE STENGLE and JOHN RABY
description: Federal and local authorities plan to increase police presence in a Dallas entertainment district after deadly shootings over the weekend. Three shootings left four people dead and 15 injured early Sunday. Authorities are still searching for suspects and motives. Nationwide, Halloween weekend saw multiple mass shootings. In Jackson, Mississippi, two people were killed and six injured during a nightclub shooting. Birmingham, Alabama, saw two shootings outside a college football game, leaving one dead and eight injured. Police in college towns reported shootings in their nightlife districts where annual Halloween gatherings are popular, including in Fayetteville, Arkansas; Newark, Delaware; Bloomington, Illinois; and Bloomington, Indiana.
headline: Law enforcement to beef up in Dallas entertainment district after shootings and nationwide violence

author: MICHAEL CASEY
description: Lindsay Clancy returned to court in a bid to dismiss the charges that she murdered her three children. The hearing Monday is the second time the Massachusetts mother has been in court since her trial ended with a deadlocked jury. Clancy has never disputed killing her three young children in 2023, but her lawyer has argued she had postpartum psychosis and was unable to control her behavior. Prosecutors have acknowledged that the 36-year-old Clancy had mental health problems but said she acted deliberately and understood her actions were wrong. A judge declared a mistrial Sept. 4 after jurors were unable to agree on a verdict.
headline: Lindsay Clancy returns to court in a bid to dismiss charges she killed her three young children

author: The Associated Press
description: Michael Wilbon is taking a break from ESPN's "Pardon the Interruption" because of health issues. The 67-year-old Wilbon announced he is dealing with multiple concerns but declined to go into further detail. Wilbon shared that people in his personal life noticed worrisome signs in recent years that he ignored. Wilbon expressed gratitude for the support from his colleagues and said he is looking forward to returning to sparring with co-host Tony Kornheiser. “PTI,” which revolutionized the TV sports debate format, recently celebrated its 25th anniversary on the network.
headline: Longtime journalist and ESPN commentator Michael Wilbon is taking a leave of absence

author: JOHN RABY
description: Mass shootings over the Halloween weekend across the U.S. in largely nightlife districts left at least six people dead and dozens injured. Police in Dallas, where the worst violence occurred, say four people are dead and 15 were injured following separate shootings in a nightlife district. Separately, police in college towns like Fayetteville, Arkansas; Birmingham, Alabama; Newark, Delaware, and Bloomington, Illinois, also reported shootings in their nightlife districts this weekend.
headline: Mass shootings over Halloween weekend leave at least 6 dead and dozens injured across US

author: BARBARA ORTUTAY and CLAUDIA CIOBANU
description: Meta is delaying new terms for business accounts after a backlash from media companies and open-web advocates. The terms, set for October 30, would allow Meta to use automated tools to scrape data from business accounts. Critics argue this could lead to Meta building competing services using the scraped content. A Norwegian court recently suspended the terms, and the UK is investigating. Meta insists the terms are about accurate product information, not news scraping. Despite Meta removing the word "train" from the terms, European critics remain unsatisfied, emphasizing the impact on journalism and media diversity.
headline: Meta delays new business terms after outcry over potential web scraping of news sites

author: STAN CHOE
description: A morning rally for U.S. stocks petered out as the tech and AI industries remained shaky following their sell-off last week. The S&P 500 fell 0.5% Monday after erasing a gain that reached 1.1% early in the day. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.4%, while the Nasdaq composite fell 1.1%. The mixed performance for indexes came even though the majority of stocks within the S&P 500 climbed. They benefited from a 7.6% drop for the price of a barrel of Brent crude. Nvidia and Alphabet swung from early gains to losses and helped drag the S&P 500 with them.
headline: More drops for AI and tech stocks overshadow gains for most of Wall Street

author: SOPHIE BATES
description: The parents of a 1-year-old boy who was shot and killed by a police officer in Mississippi have demanded a meeting with the state official who ruled that the shooting was justified. Kohen Wiley’s parents and a small group of activists led a protest Monday at the office of Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch. Kohen was killed in June when a police officer in the small town of Senatobia fired his gun into a moving vehicle while responding to a shoplifting call. Kohen was with his mom and a friend, both of whom are Black. The protesters were met in the lobby by Fitch’s chief of staff, who said Fitch was not in the office.
headline: Parents of 1-year-old fatally shot by police protest at Mississippi Attorney General's Office

author: DAVID FISCHER and JOSH FUNK
description: An investigator says parts of a business jet likely started to break off before the aircraft crashed in South Florida, killing nine people. National Transportation Safety Board member Tom Chapman said Monday that evidence found at the crash site indicates the aircraft started to break up in the air and that debris could be found far from the crash site. The plane took off from Austin, Texas, on Sunday headed for the Bahamas and crashed in Greenacres near West Palm Beach. Chapman says the weather will be a major focus of the investigation. Rain pounded the region Sunday and one of the pilots reported ice conditions at a high altitude.
headline: Parts of a Learjet may have broken off midair before Florida crash that killed 9, investigators say

author: DÁNICA COTO
description: One of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders has written the U.N. Secretary General and requested that the organization deploy a delegation to Haiti for dialogue and mediation as clashes between gangs and an international force intensify. Wilson Joseph, best known as Lanmò Sanjou and leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, sent the letter on Nov. 1, and the U.N. has received it. The letter is datelined from Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, where a group of four Salvadoran aviation technicians were attacked on Oct. 18 and remain missing.
headline: Powerful Haitian gang leader tells AP he wrote UN seeking dialogue as clashes intensify

author: MICHELLE L. PRICE and STEVE PEOPLES
description: Less than 24 hours before polls opened across America, Democrats are fighting to stay focused on the economy amid intraparty drama in the Midwest. And in Washington, President Donald Trump is promoting construction projects in the nation's capital and casting his Democratic opponents as dangerous radicals. The dueling closing messages come as the nation’s two major parties battled for control of Congress and key governor’s offices. The outcome could fundamentally reshape Trump’s final two years in office. Overall, Democrats were overwhelmingly optimistic about their party’s chances on Tuesday and Trump acknowledged that the midterm election may not go well for him or his party.
headline: Reflecting Pool vs the state of the economy: Trump and Dems clash in closing messages

author: MATTHEW LEE
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio has met with his Venezuelan counterpart in Washington. The meeting with Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco on Monday took place as the Trump administration has stepped up efforts to press the country’s interim government and opposition groups to make quick progress on preparations for elections that could be held next year. Two weeks ago, Venezuelan authorities and opposition figures agreed on a blueprint to reform the country’s electoral process to allow for free and fair elections to be held at some point in 2027. It's one of the highest-level encounters between a senior Trump administration official and a counterpart from acting President Delcy Rodríguez’s government.
headline: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as US presses for progress on election preparations

author: BRETT MARTEL
description: Saddiq Bey scored 25 points in a reserve role, Jeremiah Fears added 20 points, and the New Orleans Pelicans beat the Atlanta Hawks 121-99. Zion Williamson and Trey Murphy III each scored 15 for New Orleans, which won its second straight after losing its first four games. CJ McCollum, playing in New Orleans for the first time since the Pelicans traded him to Washington in June 2025, scored 14 points for Atlanta. Hawks reserve guard Kingston Flemmings, who scored 12 points, received a technical foul and was ejected for elbowing Bryce McGowans in the face during the game's final minutes.
headline: Saddiq Bey and Jeremiah Fears lead the Pelicans past the Hawks, 121-99

author: Tamar Hallerman
description: This is the second year of major premium increases. Enrollment in Georgia Access is down one-third since Jan. 1. Open enrollment began Sunday.
headline: Georgians should expect higher prices as they shop for ACA plans

author: CHARLES ODUM
description: Coach Kevin Stefanski, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees and the Atlanta Falcons asked too much of Michael Penix Jr. against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Sunday’s 16-0 loss at Tampa Bay was played in a driving rain. The soggy conditions were best suited for a run-dominant plan but Penix threw 24 passes while NFL rushing leader Bijan Robinson had only 19 carries. Penix made poor decisions and at times appeared to have little control of his passes. He badly missed an open Kyle Pitts on one pass. He threw four interceptions after entering the game with only one for the season.
headline: Stefanski, Rees and Falcons ask too much of Penix and passing game in loss mired by 4 interceptions

The high court refused Monday to intervene in a case involving 20,000 people the Republican administration flagged as likely noncitizens on the largely Democratic state’s voter rolls. It was the latest in a flurry of election-related litigation the day before the midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress for the last two years of Trump’s second term.

author: The Associated Press

At the same time, Democrats began to fracture in Michigan, risking their effort to retake the Senate. Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former opponent in the U.S. Senate primary, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials Sunday by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers as Democratic tensions boiled over days before the election.

author: The Associated Press

Elsewhere, Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s former primary opponent for the U.S. Senate, Haley Stevens, stunned party officials by endorsing Republican Mike Rogers. That came after the Democrat Stevens was uninvited to a joint event the same day with El-Sayed. Trump said Sunday in Iowa that he would love for Stevens to switch political parties.

In South Africa’s case, it’s another sanction against Africa’s biggest economy by the Trump administration. AGOA, the African Growth and Opportunity Act, was introduced by Democratic President Bill Clinton in 2000 to give some African nations duty-free access to the American market for some goods.

Adam Hamilton is trying to become the first Kansas Democrat to win a Senate seat in 94 years. The rallies mark Trump's return after a brief break Saturday. His parents said Tuesday that no one from the federal government has given them any substantial information. Michael and Susan Pretti say the government has responded with “cruelty” and they are calling for the Department of Justice to hold those who shot Pretti accountable. headline: Alex Pretti's parents say federal government is shielding agents involved in his killing

description: Malaysia's customs department has seized 30 servers with advanced AI chips in a suspected export-control violation. Authorities believe a syndicate is using Malaysia as a transit hub to re-export these chips to another Asian country. Malaysia introduced permit requirements last year for exporting high-performance AI chips of U.S. origin. This move came amid U.S. pressure to prevent sensitive technology from reaching China. The shipment, worth about $12.2 million, was intercepted at the main airport's free trade zone on October 15. The servers were falsely declared as electric components to avoid detection. The case is still under investigation.
headline: Malaysia seizes servers with advanced AI chips suspected of violating export controls

author: BARBARA ORTUTAY
description: Any time a company looks to start selling shares on Wall Street, it’s required to disclose potential risks for investors. In the case of artificial intelligence giant Anthropic, that has included the possibility that its products could threaten nothing less than humanity itself. The risks laid out by the San Francisco company in its filing Monday with the Securities and Exchange Commission range from the mundane to involvement in cyberattacks and the spread of dangerous misinformation. In selling itself to investors, Anthropic presents its own initial public offering as a step toward mitigating the risks it believes AI poses.
headline: Risks spelled out for Anthropic investors include blowback from runaway AI

author: CATHY BUSSEWITZ
description: Companies have been slashing jobs to invest in artificial intelligence, raising anxiety among workers who fear they may lose their livelihoods to machines. But sometimes replacing workers with AI doesn’t work out, because the tools can’t do the job as well as their human predecessors, and those companies wind up quietly rehiring workers for the positions they eliminated. Management experts suggest figuring out your competitive edge as a human and emphasizing skills such as empathy, ethics, judgment and institutional knowledge. Workers who are asked back to a company can request a contract to feel more secure.
headline: What to consider if a company that made AI-related job cuts wants you back

author: JENNIFER PELTZ
description: A onetime West Point cadet drugged his pregnant girlfriend in her barracks, gave her abortion pills while she was knocked out and caused a miscarriage. Then he went on to study at two Ivy League universities, starting at one of them after he pleaded guilty to assault. That's according to court records and a new lawsuit filed by the woman in New York last week. Caleb Suh pleaded guilty in June to the March 2022 assault. The victim was 19 at the time and in her second year at the U.S. Military Academy. Suh is scheduled to be sentenced in January.
headline: A West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend to force an unwanted abortion. Then he went to grad school

author: GARY FIELDS
description: A judge has complicated President Donald Trump’s efforts to plow forward on construction of a memorial arch, setting multiple notification deadlines before any work can begin. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, who is overseeing a lawsuit challenging the Trump administration plans, said Monday she must be told of any decision by the National Capital Planning Commission within an hour. The order set the same time limits for any decision by the National Park Service and the Department of the Interior. All three are part of a process the administration laid out in notifying the court of its plans to begin construction pending approval of the project Nov. 5 by the National Capital Planning Commission.
headline: Judge complicates construction timeline on Trump's memorial arch project with multiple deadlines

author: HYUNG-JIN KIM and KIM TONG-HYUNG
description: North Korea has denied its involvement in the recent cryptocurrency heist at Binance, dismissing as “a trite provocation” a U.S. announcement that North Korean hackers were behind the incident. Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. The FBI later said the theft was orchestrated by North Korean hackers. On Tuesday, Kim Yo Jong, the influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, called the FBI announcement “a trite provocation” and “absurd rhetoric.”
headline: North Korea denies involvement in Binance hack and criticizes FBI probe as 'a trite provocation'

author: DÁNICA COTO
description: One of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders has written the U.N. Secretary General and requested that the organization deploy a delegation to Haiti for dialogue and mediation as clashes between gangs and an international force intensify. Wilson Joseph, best known as Lanmò Sanjou and leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, sent the letter on Nov. 1, and the U.N. has received it. The letter is datelined from Plaine du Cul-de-Sac, where a group of four Salvadoran aviation technicians were attacked on Oct. 18 and remain missing.
headline: Powerful Haitian gang leader tells AP he wrote UN seeking dialogue as clashes intensify

author: DEREK GATOPOULOS and SUSIE BLANN
description: Ukrainian authorities say 26 people have been killed in Russian bomb attacks on an aid distribution center and neighboring shelter in southern Ukraine. The attacks came after a limited ceasefire expired Monday in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region. The ceasefire agreement between Ukraine and Russia had allowed humanitarian aid and evacuation missions into front-line areas in Russian-occupied territory. Earlier in the day, Ukraine and Russia reported cyberattacks on their emergency alert apps. In Ukraine, users received false warnings of dangerously high radiation levels, a chemical threat and public disturbances in Kyiv. Russian officials said hackers had sent fake alerts through its emergency ministry’s app.
headline: Russia bombs aid center and shelter in southern Ukraine, killing 26, officials say

author: EMMA BURROWS
description: Britain’s cyber chief says the U.K. is likely to face artificial intelligence cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028. On Tuesday, Richard Horne warned that criminals and states like China and Russia will increasingly use AI in their cyber activities. This could include AI-powered malware for ransomware attacks. He emphasized that outdated technology could lead to severe consequences, like empty shelves and power outages. The National Cyber Security Center's report highlights China's sophisticated cyber activity and Russia's strategic campaigns. The report urges U.K. organizations to invest in cybersecurity, noting the annual cost of cyberattacks is nearly $20 billion.
headline: UK cyber chief says the UK will face AI cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028

author: Todd Holcomb
description: This is the first meeting between Valdosta and Lowndes in which both had Top 5 rankings since 1996.
headline: Lowndes-Valdosta football rivalry is ‘biggest in the country,’ coach says

author: Todd Holcomb
description: Model is one of only seven GHSA teams that have improved their regular-season victory total by five or more.
headline: Model football coach on turnaround season: ‘We never lost the locker room’

author: Daniel Flick
description: Before the Falcons fly to Madrid for a Week 9 bout with the Cincinnati Bengals, here are five fast thoughts on Atlanta’s third loss in its last four games.
headline: 5 final thoughts from Falcons’ loss to Bucs

author: Caitlyn Stroh-Page
description: In their fifth season under Travis Noland, the Dragons won their fifth straight region championship with a 27-17 win over North Oconee.
headline: Jefferson football coach Travis Noland on region title, PSR

author: Rodney Ho
description: Films starring Mark Wahlberg and Nicolas Cage began production in Georgia within the past month.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in April 2025?

author: Rodney Ho
description: Georgia's current rate of TV and film production is much slower than during its peak times in the late 2010s and early 2020s as more films move to Europe.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in May 2025?

author: Rodney Ho
description: As of this past weekend, the Georgia Film Office has 25 active film and TV productions on its list, which has been typical over the past 12 months.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in June 2025?

author: Rodney Ho
description: The Georgia film office has just 22 active shows or movies listed on its website, down from 25 a month ago. It's been nearly a year since the total exceeded 30.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in July 2025?

author: Rodney Ho
description: This year has been a dismally slow one for TV and film production in the state of Georgia and August has shown no signs of revival.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in August 2025?

author: Rodney Ho
description: "Stranger Things" actor working on Netflix rom-com; in metro Atlanta, while "Scary Movie 6" begins filming with many of the original stars.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in September? Netflix rom-com with Millie Bobby Brown.

author: Rodney Ho
description: The new normal is steady but far from the activity of peak times. The Georgia film office lists 25 active TV and film projects as of Oct. 29, 2025. A year ago, it was 29.
headline: What’s filming now in Georgia: October 2025

author: Rodney Ho
description: "Tyler Perry's Beauty in Black," faith-based Taraji P. Henson movie and Southern Gothic crime series are among the 29 productions filming this month in the state.
headline: Tyler Perry series, "Different World" reboot among what's filming in Georgia

author: Rodney Ho
description: The January list of active TV and film productions in Georgia features the return of "Chad Powers," a reboot of "A Different World" and a bit of "Road House 2."
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in January? ‘Chad Powers’ and Glen Powell return.

author: Rodney Ho
description: Anthony Mackie, Sharon Stone, Emma Roberts and Ashley Judd are shooting this month in the state, according to our monthly update on filming in Georgia.
headline: Anthony Mackie, Emma Roberts have projects filming soon in Atlanta

author: Rodney Ho
description: The number of Georgia productions listed on the film office site edged over 30 for the first time since late spring of 2024.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia now? ‘Love is Blind,’ ‘Sistas,’ ‘Family Feud’

author: Rodney Ho
description: it was an unusually dead month for TV and film starts. The only new production listed on the Georgia film office site between March 6 and April 7 has been was “Puzzled.”
headline: What’s filming in Georgia in April: John Cho film, Damon Wayans Jr. pilot

author: Rodney Ho
description: Pete Davidson of "Saturday Night Live" fame will be in Atlanta over the summer to shoot a movie about a mafia man, Tommy Pitera, called "Tommy Karate."
headline: Pete Davidson to return to Atlanta to play notorious mobster ‘Tommy Karate’

author: Rodney Ho
description: From “Superman” at Trilith Studios to Netflix’s live action “Scooby-Doo” and a Kevin Bacon pilot, Georgia is hosting 26 film and TV productions across the state.
headline: Georgia’s film scene remains steady in May with ‘Superman,’ ‘Scooby-Doo’

author: Rodney Ho
description: The Georgia film office lists only 20 active productions, down from 26 a month ago. Productions include "The Ms. Pat Show" and "Turpentine."
headline: What’s filming in Georgia now? Shows with Ms. Pat, Connor Storrie.

author: Rodney Ho
description: A monthly update on what's shooting in Georgia shows production has reached a low point during the start of the summer with just 12 active films and TV shows.
headline: Georgia sees fewer TV, films shooting in state

author: Rodney Ho
description: Georgia film production picked up in August from July, with Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and Kristen Stewart coming to town for different productions.
headline: What’s filming in Georgia? Films with the Rock, Kristen Stewart, Pete Davidson.

author: Rodney Ho
description: Atlanta resident Dayo Okeniyi discusses why he likes the city and what he enjoys about his role as Leighton Vance in Apple TV’s “Dark Matter.”
headline: Atlanta actor Dayo Okeniyi explores endless multiverses in ‘Dark Matter’

author: Rodney Ho
description: Georgia film and TV production activity remains in relatively modest gear.
headline: What’s filming now in Georgia: ‘Will Trent,’ new Dennis Quaid show, more

author: Rodney Ho
description: David Harbour and John Cena, two actors who have spent plenty of time in metro Atlanta shooting films and TV shows, are set to star in “The Family Disappears.”
headline: David Harbour, John Cena to film ‘The Family Disappears’ in metro Atlanta

author: Emma Hurt
description: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport is about halfway through a nearly seven-year project to expand Concourse D with higher ceilings and new restrooms.
headline: Atlanta airport’s Concourse D expansion offers view of past and future

author: Emma Hurt
description: The new gates represent the largest part of the new Concourse D to open to the public — and are “only a glimpse of what’s to come," an airport official said.
headline: Atlanta airport's Concourse D extension offers a 'glimpse' of the future

author: Jewel Wicker - For the AJC
description: State Farm Arena's conversion team assembles and reassembles the basketball court, constructs and deconstructs stages, arranges and rearranges floor seating for each event.
headline: Inside the team that transforms Atlanta's State Farm Arena overnight for event

author: Zachary Hansen
description: There weren’t many evenings when the lights were dim at Atlanta's State Farm Arena during the past year.
headline: State Farm Arena ranks among busiest event venues worldwide in 2025

author: Savannah Sicurella
description: The internal investigation began after financial irregularities were discovered at the High Museum of Art before Thanksgiving.
headline: High Museum of Art exec resigns amid probe into missing funds

author: Emma Hurt
description: Delta has seen a recent spike in delays and cancellations due to a pilot staffing crunch and scheduling issues.
headline: Delta looks to hire Spirit pilots

author: Emma Hurt
description: Atlanta passengers are still left with a net loss in seats and only two ultra-low cost carriers.
headline: After Spirit exit, other airlines flood into its former Atlanta routes

author: Savannah Sicurella
description: The Atlanta-based airline offered the budget carrier a $12 million one-time fee for use of the space.
headline: Delta submits bid for Spirit Airlines’ gates, space at the Atlanta airport

author: Savannah Sicurella
description: Film and television projects spent about $2 billion in Georgia in the 12 months that ended June 30, according to numbers from the Georgia Film Office.
headline: Georgia film and TV production spending hits 10-year low

author: Zachary Hansen
description: Hyundai is evaluating plans to increase the annual production capacity at its plant near Savannah, which could result in it surpassing Tesla’s factory in Fremont, California.
headline: Georgia could soon be home to America’s most productive auto factory

author: Olivia Wakim
description: Common Thread chef Joseph Harrison will helm the Buckhead fine dining restaurant.
headline: Aria’s new executive chef is James Beard nominee from Savannah

author: Henri Hollis
description: While it’s a white-tablecloth restaurant, it’s anything but stuffy. The personable, highly professional staff creates the atmosphere of a fun dinner party.
headline: Aria in Buckhead has a new owner, same great food

author: Grace Donnelly
description: Desiree White shared her journey on social media — from taking out a transmission at home to cars she worked on across metro Atlanta as she launched a mobile mechanic service.
headline: She fixed cars as a side hustle. Now it’s a nearly million-dollar business.

author: Rosie Manins
description: Brady Lum, the museum’s former chief operating officer accused of using $600,000 for personal expenses, was granted a $10,000 bond.
headline: Former High Museum of Art executive pleads not guilty to theft of $600K

author: Adam Van Brimmer
description: Georgia Quick Start, a state-funded workforce development program, trains workers for a Hyundai EV manufacturing campus considered a test bed for the factory of tomorrow.
headline: Hyundai’s Georgia Metaplant uses Quick Start to train workers

author: Joe Kovac Jr.
description: New $350 million, 10,000-plus-capacity venue to replace nearly 60-year-old Macon Coliseum in city that spawned Little Richard, Otis Redding and other famous Georgia musicians.
headline: New $350 million Georgia arena to replace storied Macon Coliseum

author: Rosie Manins
description: Drive Planning founder and CEO Todd Burkhalter was sentenced to prison Friday for what federal prosecutors say was Georgia’s largest Ponzi scheme.
headline: CEO of Alpharetta investment firm sentenced to prison in Ponzi scheme

author: MARK KENNEDY
description: Stephen Graham dives into the mind of a serial killer for his role in the new Apple TV series “Nocturne.” He binged on true crime documentaries, handpicked by his wife, to prepare for the role. The series is based on Lars Kepler novels. It premieres Friday. It follows a kidnapped teen who resurfaces after three years, while his sister remains missing. Graham plays Jurek Walter, an imprisoned murderer who manipulates those around him. The show features a retired detective, played by Liev Schreiber, and an undercover FBI agent, portrayed by Zazie Beetz. The creators aim to offer a fresh take on the genre.
headline: A serial killer, an obsessed cop and an undercover FBI agent. Welcome to Apple's 'Nocturne'

author: Taylor Croft
description: Andy Stanley announced he is stepping down as senior pastor of Atlanta's North Point Ministries next year.
headline: Andy Stanley to step down as senior pastor from North Point Ministries

description: Brad Keselowski has been granted permission to pursue other NASCAR racing opportunities for the 2027 season and will sell his 20% equity stake in Roush Fenway Keselowski Racing. Keselowski announced a month ago that he was leaving the team he joined as a driver, competition executive and part-owner five years ago, but he had been restricted from exploring rides with other teams despite his driving contract expiring after 2026. He said the team granted him a verbal release Saturday, an hour before his news conference at Martinsville Speedway, and he is allowed to drive for any team or manufacturer next season.
headline: Brad Keselowski granted release to explore NASCAR rides, will sell stake in RFK Racing

author: Asia Simone Burns
description: A man fatally shot his wife, two adult sons and a girlfriend of one of his sons in an apparent South Georgia murder-suicide, Douglas police say.
headline: 5 dead in apparent murder-suicide at South Georgia home, police say

author: Kelly Yamanouchi
description: Federal regulators last year accused First Liberty of operating a $140 million Ponzi scheme that targeted conservative and faith-based investors across Georgia and beyond.
headline: Feds seek 14 years for First Liberty leader as supporters urge leniency

author: Taylor Croft
description: An Atlanta charter school educator died this week when he was ejected from a roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, which officials said is scheduled to reopen Friday.
headline: Six Flags Over Georgia incident leaves 1 dead, several injured

author: DIDI TANG
description: Analysts at Graphika report that the influence campaign known as Spamouflage is active ahead of the midterm elections. Accounts likely linked to China are posing as U.S. voters and posting divisive content about politics and social issues. On Friday, Graphika identified Spamouflage-linked activity on X that resembles tactics seen in 2024 before the U.S. presidential election. Intelligence officials have long warned about online influence operations by Russia, China, and Iran targeting U.S. voters. Darren Linvill from Clemson University says Spamouflage is ineffective at mimicking Americans but is more successful at suppressing information and harassing the Chinese diaspora.
headline: Graphika finds China-linked Spamouflage accounts posing as US voters on X

author: Taylor Croft
description: Big Blue Marble Academy in Grovetown has had previous incidents involving physical mistreatment of children in recent years, state reports show.
headline: Grovetown daycare where child was hurt has history of mistreatment, records show

author: Vanessa McCray
description: Three people were injured in a shooting Saturday in the tailgate area of an Augusta high school, according to the Richmond County Sheriff's Office.
headline: Woman arrested in homecoming shooting at Augusta high school, officials say

author: JEFFREY COLLINS and GENE JOHNSON
description: Police in South Carolina say they have closed their investigation into the overdose death of actor Hayden Panettiere following a coroner’s findings that it was accidental. No charges were filed. Greenville police said Wednesday in a statement the decision was based on the medical examiner’s determination as well as the findings of the investigation. The former star of the TV series “Heroes” and “Nashville” was pronounced dead in an apartment in Greenville on Aug. 16 at age 36 after paramedics found her unresponsive. It remains unclear whether federal agents are still looking into her death separately.
headline: South Carolina police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after coroner's ruling

author: BETH HARRIS
description: Scott Clifton of “The Bold and the Beautiful” and Tamara Tunie of “Beyond the Gates” have won lead acting honors at the Daytime Emmy Awards. It's Clifton's second career trophy in the lead category. Tunie made her return to the soap opera genre after 17 years away. “General Hospital” won its record 19th trophy overall as outstanding drama and sixth in a row. Roger Howarth and Beth Maitland of “The Young and the Restless” swept the supporting acting categories. Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, lost in the lifestyle program category for her former Netflix show “With Love, Meghan.”
headline: Scott Clifton and Tamara Tunie earn lead acting Daytime Emmys. 'General Hospital' wins again

author: MARC LEVY
description: Utah is pursuing criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and two executives, after a federal judge rejected Kalshi’s effort to prevent Utah from enforcing its anti-gambling laws against the activity. The felony charges filed Wednesday could represent a new tactic in how states try to assert regulatory authority over the fast-expanding activity. The charges include 13 counts of violating the state’s prohibition on gambling and another charge involving profiting off illegal activity. The defendants are Kalshi and its co-founders, chief executive officer Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara. Kalshi called the charges a “crazy overreach” and said it looks forward to “putting a stop to this in court.”
headline: Utah charges Kalshi and its founders, escalating a fight over who can regulate prediction markets

author: JOE REEDY
description: Zac Taylor has learned from previous international games and is taking the Cincinnati Bengals to Madrid earlier for their game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Bengals will leave Tuesday to get acclimated before Sunday's game. Taylor wants the team to maintain momentum after three straight wins. Cincinnati is off to a strong start this season. The Bengals are focusing on improving their early game performance, having rallied from deficits in recent weeks. Taylor also sees the trip as a chance to expand their fan base in Europe. Despite the travel, the main goal remains to win and improve to 6-2.
headline: A Tuesday flight and a 6-day week: Bengals tweak their Madrid routine for Falcons

author: RONALD BLUM
description: New York Yankees closer David Bednar, Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki and Seattle outfielder Randy Arozarena were among eight players who received $23.15 million qualifying offers from their teams. Milwaukee first baseman/outfielder Jake Bauers and Baltimore left-hander Trevor Rogers also received the offers along with Minnesota catcher Ryan Jeffers, Pittsburgh second baseman Brandon Lowe and San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon. Players have until Nov. 17 to accept. Qualifying offers began after the 2012 season, and only 18 of 157 prior offers have been accepted. The figure is determined by the average of the top 125 major league contracts this year.
headline: Bednar, Suzuki and Arozarena are among 8 MLB players receiving $23.15 million qualifying offers

author: KRISTIN M. HALL and HANNAH SCHOENBAUM
description: Tennessee prosecutors have released video of National Guard troops pointing their handguns at a man as he lay dying on a Memphis sidewalk last summer after a guard member shot him in the back. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation continues to investigate the shooting of Tyrin Johnson on July 5. No charges have been filed. Johnson had been armed and died at the scene from a single gunshot wound, according to investigators. The guard members were part of a federal task force created by President Donald Trump, who last year sent troops and federal agents to Democrat-run cities that he described as overrun with crime.
headline: Bodycam video shows aftermath of fatal shooting by National Guard in Memphis

author: LINDSEY BAHR
description: The North American box office faced a slump this weekend as Halloween festivities drew people away from theaters. The Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything” led ticket sales, just edging out the DC Studios movie “Clayface.” Studio estimates on Sunday suggested total earnings would not surpass $56 million, marking it as the second lowest weekend of the year. “You Can See Everything” earned $10.6 million from 2,655 locations in its third weekend. “Clayface” trailed by only $200,684. Laika’s animated film “Wildwood” claimed third place with $7.5 million. Despite the dip, the domestic box office remains up over 17% from last year.
headline: Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything,’ 'Clayface' lead sleepy Halloween weekend

description: Dodge is returning to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, a year earlier than initially expected. The Stellantis-owned Dodge brand announced its return at the SEMA Show in Las Vegas on Monday. Dodge will once again give the Cup Series four manufacturers, joining Chevrolet, Ford and Toyota in fielding entries to compete in a 36-race schedule that begins in mid-February and crowns a champion in early November. Kaulig Racing will use the Dodge Charger to field a two-car team beginning at the Daytona 500. AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon are expected to fill those seats.
headline: Dodge announces its return to the NASCAR Cup Series beginning at the Daytona 500

author: COREY WILLIAMS, JACQUELINE GANUN and JOEY CAPPELLETTI
description: Michigan Democrats are scrambling to refocus voters' attention and move past a stunning defection in one of the nation’s most closely watched Senate races. Rep. Haley Stevens, who lost the Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed, endorsed Republican Mike Rogers on Sunday, prompting her expulsion from the state party. The move exposed lingering divisions over El-Sayed, particularly among Jewish and Black voters. But Democrats, including longtime Stevens allies, condemned her decision and said Monday it had energized their base. El-Sayed reported raising $2.4 million Sunday, while party officials described a surge in volunteers. More than 2.3 million Michigan voters have already cast ballots.
headline: El-Sayed, Michigan Democrats push to galvanize voters after stunning Senate race defection

author: NATE RYAN
description: Kyle Larson salvaged a nearly disastrous Sunday at Martinsville Speedway, putting him on the cusp of his second consecutive NASCAR Cup Series championship. With a ninth-place finish at Martinsville, Larson lost only six points off his massive lead in the championship and leads by 67 points over Christopher Bell (who was 10th) heading into the Nov. 8 season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. While Larson struggled, Hendrick Motorsports teammates William Byron and Chase Elliott made it a sweep of the top two spots.
headline: Kyle Larson closes in on NASCAR championship as Hendrick teammate William Byron wins at Martinsville

author: NATE RYAN
description: Kyle Larson holds a 67-point lead in the Chase and should be able to cruise to a NASCAR Cup Series championship in the season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Although he has excelled at the 1.5-mile oval with two victories in the past four races, Larson says he’s feeling the pressure of closing out his second consecutive title over the Joe Gibbs Racing duo of Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin. Larson needs only nine points to clinch the title outright. Larson says “it’s not locked up, so there’s still definitely pressure.”
headline: Kyle Larson still feels NASCAR championship pressure despite comfortable lead for Homestead finale

author: Greg Bluestein
description: Federal prosecutors charged the founder of Newnan-based First Liberty Building & Loan on Thursday, escalating a sprawling civil fraud case into a criminal prosecution.
headline: First Liberty founder Brant Frost IV charged with wire fraud

author: HANNA ARHIROVA and DEREK GATOPOULOS
description: Officials say that a six-day ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in southern Ukraine has held for its first day and night. The truce began Tuesday and aims to provide food, medicine and evacuation for about 2,000 residents. It will be the first significant truce since Russia’s full-scale invasion began nearly five years ago. That's if it's successful. U.S. first lady Melania Trump brokered the humanitarian mission and Pope Leo XIV urged the provision of aid and safe evacuations. The war rages on elsewhere with Russian drone strikes in Kharkiv and Ukrainian drones downed in Russia.
headline: A ceasefire in a Ukrainian city is holding, officials say, as Moscow and Kyiv await US-led talks

author: HANNA ARHIROVA and VOLODYMYR YURCHUK
description: A localized ceasefire in Oleshky, Ukraine, held for a third day and humanitarian aid is expected to arrive soon. The truce between Russia and Ukraine, which began Tuesday, is allowing military units to clear some landmines, and aid deliveries are expected to begin Friday. The ceasefire in the Russian-held southern Ukraine city has also brought calm to nearby Kherson city, and both sides thanked U.S. first lady Melania Trump for helping broker it. No ceasefire violations have been reported. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy meanwhile condemned a Russian drone attack that hit two passenger trains in central Ukraine Thursday, killing at least 14 people. Russia says it downed 1,214 Ukrainian drones.
headline: Aid mission set to enter Oleshky as a localized Russia-Ukraine truce holds for a third day

author: KAITLYN HUAMANI
description: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a potential security issue that appears to be a hack. The company said late Thursday the estimated total impact was at roughly $6.3 billion, which could be one of the most significant such security incidents on record. The extent of the damage is unclear, but stablecoin issuers froze funds Thursday evening. Binance assures users their funds are safe and is reviewing information urgently. Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle froze significant amounts in response to the incident. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, who stepped down as CEO after pleading guilty to a felony, said user funds are safe but acknowledged the situation looks like a hack. Bitcoin's price dropped 3.2% Thursday evening.
headline: Binance flags 'potential security issue,' says approximately $6.3 billion impacted

author: BERNARD CONDON
description: The FBI says the billions of dollars stolen from Binance within minutes in the biggest crypto heist in history was orchestrated by North Korean hackers. The bureau says this week's attack was tied to “malicious cyber activity” by an entity known as TraderTraitor. That same entity behind a $1.5 billion Bybit hack last year. The FBI said Saturday that it is advising crypto exchanges, blockchain analytics companies and others to block transactions tied to certian addresses to keep the money from being laundered further. Later Saturday night, President Donald Trump said authorities were still learning about the case, however, and added, “We don't know if it was North Korea.”
headline: FBI blames North Korea for stolen billions from Binance in biggest hack in history

author: SAVANNAH PETERS and MEAD GRUVER
description: The Four Corners region of the Southwestern U.S. is warily eyeing a forecast for still more rain. That's after flooding over the past several days that has been blamed for two deaths. The latest town to evacuate is tiny Bluff in southeastern Utah, after San Juan River flooding swamped parts of cities and towns upstream in Colorado and New Mexico. The town of 250 had a surge overnight Sunday and Monday, bringing the flood toll there to 17 homes and five businesses. Hundreds of homes upstream in New Mexico and Colorado remain evacuated and without power. New Mexico officials peg damages as high as $300 million in their state alone.
headline: Flood-weary US Southwest eyes forecast for more rain

author: JAMIE STENGLE
description: The National Weather Service says heavy rains are expected to bring a threat of flash flooding to already saturated areas of the U.S. Southwest. The rain was expected to start Saturday evening, with the flooding threat going into Monday. As much as 4 inches of rain could fall in parts the region, where a number of weather systems have brought a deadly autumn of soaking rains. Several people were rescued from floodwaters Friday in Arizona and Nevada. Allison Santorelli, a meteorologist with the Weather Prediction Center in College Park, Maryland, said it won't take much rainfall to be impactful in some of the areas.
headline: Heavy rains expected to bring flooding risk to already saturated parts of the US Southwest

author: DAVE SKRETTA
description: A Kentucky Court of Appeals judge has denied the NCAA's request for emergency relief, allowing 30 college athletes to remain eligible as the basketball season is about to begin. The athletes, including Missouri's Mark Mitchell and LSU's Skyy Clark, received a temporary injunction on October 16. This allows them to compete while the NCAA appeals a ruling related to the new five-for-five eligibility model. Kentucky judge Sara Walter Combs said in her ruling that the NCAA failed to prove imminent harm from the injunction. The ruling also affects football players who will continue to compete for their teams.

author: BRETT MARTEL
description: LSU coach Will Wade declined on Thursday to take questions about RJ Luis Jr., who a day earlier won a temporary restraining order that could open a door for him to play for the Tigers — if Wade adds him to his roster. Wade says he already has made himself clear and that his stance has not changed. Wade has previously stated that he intended to follow “SEC protocols” regarding Luis. But a Louisiana judge's latest court order in Luis’ case ostensibly bans Wade from doing that. Specifically, the ruling temporarily bars the SEC from punishing LSU if it plays Luis. author: GARY FIELDS
description: The legal challenges to President Donald Trump’s proposed memorial arch are mounting. The District of Columbia and Virginia sued in federal court Saturday as the administration says construction could begin as early as next week. There are now three lawsuits calling for a halt to potential work on a monument that would rise 250 feet on a patch of grass off the bridge that spans the Potomac River, connecting the city with Arlington National Cemetery. U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan is already considering issuing an order to halt the project until the original lawsuit is resolved. She held a hearing Friday but didn't immediately act. Trump said Saturday night that the arch “is very important militarily for Washington D.C. and our country."
headline: Virginia and DC sue over Trump's arch, adding to legal challenges as government wants work to begin

author: KAITLYN HUAMANI and CHAN HO-HIM
description: Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, says hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit. The company said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and was beginning to recover assets for users. Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets. The cryptocurrency exchange has promised to cover all losses, and it has been sharing regular updates on its social media channels as it uncovers more information about the hack.
headline: What to know about the $6.3B hack on Binance, likely the biggest-ever crypto theft

author: GARY FIELDS
description: Donald Trump’s social media posts on the closure and renovation of a historic golf course in the nation’s capital are putting Justice Department lawyers in the uncomfortable position of explaining whether the president of the United States should be believed. U.S. Judge Ana Reyes says the department should clarify “whether any plan exists to close East Potomac Golf Course on or around November 15." She has ordered Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr. to appear in court Friday or Monday for a status hearing. Tuesday’s order is in response to Trump’s social media post late Monday criticizing Reyes' temporary injunction stopping work at the East Potomac Park.
headline: Who should be believed? Trump's social media post on golf course leads lawyers back to court

author: SUSAN MONTOYA BRYAN
description: Stockyards in New Mexico that had closed due to the New World screwworm outbreak are bustling again. The gates at the Columbus port of entry opened Monday, marking the first time since 2024 that Mexican cattle have crossed here. It's the third port to reopen since August as the U.S. Department of Agriculture works with Mexican officials to normalize cross-border livestock trading under tighter biosecurity rules. U.S. Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins says the new framework means the U.S. and Mexico are better prepared for other future biological threats. In this case, the playbook includes expanded surveillance, multiple layers of cattle inspections and the release of more than 1.6 billion sterile flies across the region.
headline: With tighter checks for flesh-eating screwworm, a border crossing reopens

author: HANNA ARHIROVA and VOLODYMYR YURCHUK
description: Civilians in Ukraine's Kherson region are preparing for the end of a localized ceasefire. The truce was brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and ends Sunday evening. It allowed evacuations in Oleshky. About 2,000 civilians were in Oleshky when the truce began. They could evacuate to Ukrainian or Russian-controlled areas or remain with replenished supplies. Russian and Ukrainian drone attacks continue meanwhile. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that Russia targets Ukraine's energy systems. That has left many without power. The local theater continues performances in Kherson to offer hope and unity.
headline: Civilians in Ukraine's Kherson prepare for the return of war as localized ceasefire ends

description: After first saying he didn't have a conflict of interest, Justice John Nielsen agreed to sit out Planned Parenthood's challenge to the Legislature's three-judge panels. The group had sought to have have Nielsen disqualified over his work for a pro-life group.

description: Utah has allowed undocumented high school graduates who have applied for legal residency to pay in-state college rates since 2002, when Utah’s Republican-dominated Legislature passed a law allowing the tuition break.

description: Sen. Mike Lee is publicly siding with President Donald Trump’s Justice Department as it investigates his state’s elections chief, a fellow Republican.

description: In Utah, the rate of immigration arrests from 2022 to this spring was higher than rates in New York and California, a new study shows.

description: As the DOJ investigates Utah's elections chief, auditors again “did not observe significant fraud” in a review of the state's most recent election.

description: Gov. Spencer Cox's nominees to fill two seats on the Supreme Court — Judge Matthew Bell and Michael Menssen — cleared a Senate committee and now await full confirmation this week.

description: The oversight is part of a larger issue, auditors said —  the failure to have safeguards that catch errors effectively.

description: Gov. Spencer Cox has now appointed more justices to the bench than any governor in Utah history.

description: A business that had received $2 million closed its new facility — which Utah’s main economic development agency didn’t know until months later, an audit found. Oversight is improving under new leadership, an auditor said.

description: At a Washington news conference, Justice Department officials used an indictment against a Utah postal worker who allegedly threw ballots away to justify attempts to crack down on mail voting.
headline: A Utah postal worker allegedly threw ballots in a church dumpster. DOJ says it justifies a crackdown on mail voting.

description: A new poll shows Utahns are souring on both President Donald Trump and Gov. Spencer Cox, with the approval ratings of both tumbling by double digits in the past year.

description: The former Utah postal worker told investigators he wanted to finish his shift early — not to disrupt an election. One voter who didn't get her ballot says his alleged actions haven't damaged her trust in voting by mail.

description: The historic Rowland Hall campus will no longer be a school, but expect it to be full of students.

description: Utah will not purge voter rolls based on a database revamped under President Donald Trump to check voters' citizenship, Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson said Friday after the U.S. Supreme Court allowed the controversial program’s deployment.

description: Amendment B on the November ballot asks voters if they want to make it more difficult to pass a ballot initiative that includes a tax increase. Critics say it undermines the constitutional right, proponents say it protects taxpayers.

description: State Rep. Trevor Lee was charged Monday with four felony counts related to alleged mortgage fraud and immediately resigned his House seat.
